meals: Broccoli Two Ways

recipes.title: Broccoli Two Ways
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash the broccoli. Cut the florets from the primary stem, leaving some stem on each floret. 2. Place 1 c (240 ml) of florets in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Store the rest for later in the week. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. 3. Cover and steam the florets. For firm florets, steam until they have brightened in color and softened slightly, but hold together when pressed, about 3 minutes in the microwave or 6 minutes on the stovetop. For soft florets, steam until they dull in color and easily mash, about 5 minutes in the microwave and 10 minutes on the stovetop. It’s okay to offer only firm or only soft florets at first. Alternatively, try both: pull a large floret from the heat when it is still firm, then continue to steam the rest until soft. 4. Mash small florets until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay. 5. Stir in hemp seeds and oil if you like. Oil adds healthy fat and flavor, and hemp seeds are suggested throughout this guide to increase iron in baby’s meal. At this age, baby’s iron stores are naturally low. At each meal, try offering an iron-rich food, like hemp seeds or another iron-rich food. See more food ideas to boost iron in baby’s diet.
recipes.howToServe: Let baby taste broccoli in two forms: mashed florets to get food in the belly, and whole florets to promote oral motor skills. Pass a large floret and let baby touch, grab, and munch. When baby is ready, offer a pre-loaded spoon of mashed floret. Hold the utensil near baby’s mouth and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed the spoon, let go.
recipes.howToStore: Keep cooked broccoli in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Gagging Is Normal: As baby begins eating solid foods, it is natural to gag. When baby gags, it is likely not an emergency and you did not do anything wrong. Gagging is a normal reflex that is also an essential learning tool to teach baby how much is “too much” when taking bites. Learn the difference between gagging and choking.

meals: Mango or Banana Two Ways

recipes.title: Mango or Banana Two Ways
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash, dry, and peel the mango. To peel a mango: cut off the bottom, place the fruit on its cut end, and run a knife or vegetable peeler down the sides to remove its skin. 2. Cut the mango along its pit to create halves, then cut the halves into long, thick spears about the size of two adult fingers pressed together. Mash 2 to 3 spears for baby’s meal. Store the remaining spears for later. 3. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top. Mango is packed with vitamin C, which helps baby’s body absorb the iron in hemp seeds and other iron-rich foods. 4. Prepare the pit: it’s a great shape for baby to hold, plus it offers plenty of fruit to munch. If you’d like to add a little grip, cut divots into the soft fruit attached to the pit. These nooks and crannies help baby hold onto the slippery food.
recipes.howToServe: Pass the mango pit to baby and encourage baby to grab and munch on the fruit. Keep in mind that if baby has a known allergy to cashew or pistachio, there is a chance that gnawing on the mango pit may trigger a rash around the mouth. The fruit itself is unlikely to cause any reaction. When baby is ready, offer a pre-loaded spoon with mashed mango. Hold the utensil near baby’s mouth and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed the spoon, let go.
recipes.howToStore: Cut mango keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Softer Foods and Gagging: It may sound counterintuitive, but softer foods like banana can cause more intense gagging than firmer foods with more resistive structure like mango pit. Why? As the gums mash, soft food spreads, clumps, and sticks in the mouth, causing baby’s gag reflex to kick in. If baby is gagging a lot at every meal or gagging to the point of vomiting at most meals, talk to a health care provider about a swallowing evaluation.

Why Bigger is Better: At this age, larger pieces of food are easier for baby to grab and bring to the mouth— a key skill in learning to self-feed. When they are firmer and more resistive, these larger foods can help baby understand the mouth’s boundaries as the child munches and moves the tongue around the food. Of course, this may not lead to much food in the belly, but the benefits are significant.

meals: Oatmeal Two Ways

recipes.title: Oatmeal Two Ways
ingredients: ½ c (96 g) dry instant oatmeal
recipes.instructions: 1. Place the instant oats in a mixing bowl. 2. Bring the water to a boil, then pour it into the bowl. Stir to combine the oats and water. Let the mixture sit until thickened and cooled, about 10 minutes. 3. Scoop a heaping spoonful (about 2 tbsp / 30 ml) of oatmeal and form it into a ball. If the oatmeal is too loose to form a ball, add a spoonful or two of instant oats to thicken the mixture. 4. Scoop some of the remaining oats from the mixing bowl into baby’s bowl. Serving size varies. Let your child decide how much to eat. If you like, stir in a spoonful of water, human milk, 5. and/or formula to loosen the oats in baby’s bowl. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the bowl and oatmeal ball to baby and let the child self-feed. When baby is ready, pre-load a spoon with oatmeal and place it in front of baby for the child to pick up. If baby needs help, pass the spoon in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Oatmeal keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. If oatmeal contains human milk, use within 4 days. Bowls or No Bowls? Either works! Many foods may be placed directly on the tray or table in front of baby— no bowl required. When a bowl feels necessary, try one with a wide, flat bottom to help prevent tipping. Bowls made of material that clings to surfaces can also help.

meals: Broccoli or Cauliflower Florets + Mashed Cannelinni Beans

recipes.title: Broccoli or Cauliflower Florets + Mashed Cannelinni Beans
recipes.yield: ¼ c (56 g) beans + ½ c (120 ml) florets
ingredients: ¼ c (60 ml) cooked cannellini beans
recipes.instructions: 1. Pull the florets from the refrigerator and use the directions on Day 1 to steam them but keep all florets whole instead of mashing some. 2. Rinse the beans. If you are using canned beans, transfer any extra beans from the can to an airtight container to store for later. 3. Mash the beans and oil in baby’s bowl until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole beans or big chunks. 4. Stick the largest floret in the mash so that it is standing up and ready for baby to grab.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the bowl and florets and let the child self-feed. To encourage the use of utensils, offer a pre-loaded spoon of mashed beans. Hold the utensil near baby’s mouth and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed the spoon, let go.
recipes.howToStore: Keep mashed cannellini beans in an air- tight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Digesting Beans: Beans + babies = gas and poop. This is normal: beans are packed with fiber and resistant starch, which help move poop along while strengthening the gut. Start small: a few baby spoonfuls get food in the belly without causing too much uncomfortable gas.

meals: Mango Two Ways

recipes.title: Mango Two Ways
recipes.instructions: 1. Peel and halve the mango. Set aside the pit to serve whole. Cut the halves into spears about the size of two adult fingers pressed together. 2. Mash 1 or 2 spears and sprinkle hemp seeds on top to boost iron in baby’s diet. 3. If you have any leftover oatmeal, stir it into the mashed mango for a nutrition boost.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the mango pit and mashed mango and let baby self-feed. If baby needs help picking up the pit, pass it in the air for the child to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cut mango keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Managing the Mess: Mess is good—that’s hard to hear when food is everywhere. When baby is covered in food, try to remember the long game: touching bumpy, cold, sticky, warm, and wet food teaches baby that food can have more than one texture—awareness that can help prevent picky eating and sensory aversions in toddlerhood. Check out ways to manage the mess.

meals: Stewed Apple Two Ways

recipes.title: Stewed Apple Two Ways
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash, peel, and halve the apple. Remove the core, seeds, and stem. 2. Place the apple halves in a small pot. Add 1 c (240 ml) of water. 3. Cover and set the pot on medium-high heat. As soon as the water begins to boil, lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook until the apple is easily pierced with a fork, about 10 minutes. Cook time varies based on the apple size. 4. Remove the apple halves from the pot. 5. Mash one apple half in baby’s bowl. If you are using oatmeal, stir it into the mashed apple. Let cool. Sprinkle hemp seeds or another iron-rich seed on top to add some of this essential nutrient to the meal.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the mashed apple and stewed apple half and let baby touch, grab, and munch on the food. It’s okay if baby chooses to play with food—play is part of learning to eat. To get some food in the belly, try this: hold a pre-loaded spoon of mashed apple in the air in front of baby and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed it, let go and watch as baby takes the lead.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked apple keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Stewed Apple and Gagging: As baby bites, the brain prompts baby to start chewing, which minimizes risk. Sometimes a too-big piece breaks off in the mouth, and when the tongue struggles to control the food, baby gags. It’s okay: this teaches baby to take smaller bites.

meals: Cauliflower Two Ways + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg

recipes.title: Cauliflower Two Ways + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cauliflower. Grab the florets from the refrigerator and use the directions on Week 1 | Day 3 to steam them. Set aside 1 or 2 of the largest florets to serve whole. Mash the rest with oil until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay. Prepare the eggs. Bring a pot of water to boil. Lower the heat to create a simmer, then gently lower the eggs into the pot. Cover the pot and cook for 12 minutes, then transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water. Set aside 1 egg for today’s meal and store the rest for later. Peel the eggshell and cut the egg into quarters. Mash 1 egg quarter with a spoonful of mashed cauliflower and a splash of water until the mixture is mostly smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no large clumps of egg. Season the remaining egg quarters with salt and pepper to eat as a snack for yourself.
recipes.howToServe: Scoop a scant amount (about the size of your fingertip) of the cauliflower-egg mash onto a spoon for baby. After baby has taken the bite, offer the large cauliflower floret for baby to munch while you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer more cauliflower-egg mash.
recipes.howToStore: Hard-boiled eggs keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 1 week. Start Early in the Day: Most allergic reactions occur within a few hours of ingestion and often within minutes. Offering a common food allergen shortly after waking leaves plenty of time to observe baby and it is easier to get in touch with your doctor should you need one.

meals: Broccoli Egg Strip

recipes.title: Broccoli Egg Strip
recipes.instructions: Prepare the broccoli. Grab the florets from the refrigerator and use the directions on Week 1 | Day 1 to steam them. Set aside the largest floret to serve whole. Finely chop the rest of the florets. Transfer the chopped florets to a mixing bowl. Prepare the egg strips. Crack the eggs into the mixing bowl with the chopped broccoli. Whisk to combine the yolks and whites with the broccoli. Warm the oil in an 8-inch non-stick skillet set on medium heat. (If you are using a larger skillet, increase the number of eggs so that the mixture covers the bottom of the pan.) When the oil shimmers, pour in the egg mixture and turn the heat to low. Cover and steam until the eggs are firm and the edges have started to curl, about 5 minutes. Transfer the omelet from the pan to a cutting board. Cut into strips about the width of two adult fingers pressed together. Let cool.
recipes.howToServe: Let baby munch on 1 egg strip and large florets as you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer another egg strip. Keep in mind that eggs often cause gagging, a natural reaction that helps teach baby how to eat solid foods.
recipes.howToStore: Egg strips keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Slow and Steady Pace: It is important to introduce one common food allergen at a time so you know which food is responsible should an allergic reaction occur. A few consecutive days of daily ingestion is usually more than enough to determine that a common food allergen is well-tolerated. That said, to maintain tolerance, the food must be continued in the diet regularly.

meals: Mango or Banana Two Ways + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg

recipes.title: Mango or Banana Two Ways + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg
recipes.instructions: Prepare the mango. Wash, dry, and peel the mango. Cut the mango along its pit to create halves, then cut the halves into long, thick spears about the size of two adult fingers pressed together. Set aside the pit and mash 2 to 3 spears for baby’s meal. Store the rest of the fruit for later. If you like, roll the mango pit in hemp seeds or another iron-rich seed to increase this essential nutrient in baby’s meal. Prepare the egg. Grab a hard-boiled egg from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 2 | Day 8 to prepare more. Peel the eggshell and cut the egg into quarters. Mash 1 egg quarter with some mashed mango until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no large clumps of egg. Season the remaining egg quarters with salt and snack on them as baby eats.
recipes.howToServe: Pre-load a baby spoon with some of the egg-mango mash for baby and offer the spoon to the child. Pass the mango pit to baby and let the child munch as you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction.
recipes.howToStore: Cut mango keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Why Egg Causes Gagging: Baby may gag while eating eggs—and this is normal. The soft texture breaks apart easily in the mouth, spreading over the tongue and occasionally clinging to the roof of the mouth, which triggers the protective gag reflex.

meals: Broccoli Egg Strip + Steamed Corn on the Cob

recipes.title: Broccoli Egg Strip + Steamed Corn on the Cob
recipes.instructions: Prepare the egg strips. Grab the egg strip from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 2 | Day 9 to prepare more. Prepare the corn. Peel and shuck the corn husk and silk. Cut off the stem and tip, then cut the cob into 2 or 3 rounds about the width of three adult fingers pressed together. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the corn cob rounds and boil until the corn has brightened in color and softened slightly, about 8 minutes. Drain. Run cold water over the corn cob rounds to cool them down for baby
recipes.howToServe: Offer 1 egg strip and corn cob rounds and let baby self-feed as you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer another egg strip.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked corn on the cob keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Why Corn Shows Up in Poop: Do not be alarmed: it is normal for bit of corn kernel to appear in baby’s poop. Corn contains insoluble fiber that holds its shape as the food passes through the digestive tract. This is not a bad sign and it doesn’t mean that baby did not get any nutrition: corn has done its job of helping move along other foods through baby’s body.

meals: Cooked Bell Pepper Half + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg

recipes.title: Cooked Bell Pepper Half + Mashed Hard-Boiled Egg
recipes.instructions: Prepare the pepper. Preheat the oven to 375 F (191 C). Line a sheet tray with parchment paper. Wash, dry, and halve the pepper. Remove the stem, seeds, and pith. Coat the pepper halves with oil. Place the pepper halves cut-side facing down on the tray. Roast until the peppers are tender but not totally collapsed, about 10 minutes. Peppers that hold their shape are easier for baby to hold—and a whole half is easier for baby to hold than small strips at this age of life. Prepare the egg. Grab a hard-boiled egg from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 2 | Day 8 to prepare more. Peel the eggshell and cut the egg into quarters. Mash 2 egg quarters with 2 or 3 spoonfuls of human milk, formula, and/or water until the mixture is mostly smooth with no large clumps of egg. Season the remaining egg quarters with salt and snack on them as baby eats.
recipes.howToServe: Pre-load a spoon with mashed egg for baby, then offer a couple more spoonfuls. Offer a bell pepper half for baby to munch while you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked bell pepper halves keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Let Baby Practice: If baby has trouble grabbing food off the table or tray, exercise patience: the simple act of trying is great practice, and touching the food is part of the journey. If baby is still struggling after a minute or two of exploration, step in to help: hold the pepper in the air in front of baby and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed it, let go.

meals: Cauliflower Florets + Sesame-Free Hummus

recipes.title: Cauliflower Florets + Sesame-Free Hummus
recipes.yield: 1 ½ c (360 ml) hummus + ½ c (120 ml) florets
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) cooked cauliflower florets
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cauliflower. Grab the florets from the refrigerator and use the directions on Week 1 | Day 3 to steam them, but keep all florets whole instead of mashing some. Prepare the hummus. Rinse the chickpeas. Halve and juice the lemon, then set aside 1 tbsp (15 ml) of juice and store the rest. Blend the chickpeas, olive oil, lemon juice, and spice until mostly smooth. You need a high-powered food processor or blender to make creamy, smooth hummus. If you don’t have one, make a chickpea mash by smashing and mixing the ingredients until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole chickpeas. Scoop ½ c (120 ml) hummus into baby’s bowl and store the rest for later.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a floret in the hummus so it is standing and ready for baby to grab, then let the child self-feed. If baby needs help, swipe a floret in the hummus and pass it in the air for baby to grab from you. If baby signals for more, swipe another floret for the child.
recipes.howToStore: Sesame-Free Hummus keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Contact Rashes vs. Allergic Reactions: Simply touching acidic foods like lemon, orange, tomato, and strawberries can cause a contact rash, a harmless skin reaction that often appears near the chin and mouth. It usually dissipates shortly after the skin is gently cleansed. Applying a barrier ointment (such as petroleum jelly or a plant-based oil/wax blend) to the face before mealtime can help minimize irritation. However, if the rash is widespread and/or associated with itchiness it may be a symptom of an allergic reaction and you should stop serving that food until you can discuss with a pediatric allergist.

meals: Apple Oatmeal Two Ways + Smooth Peanut Butter on the Fingertip

recipes.title: Apple Oatmeal Two Ways + Smooth Peanut Butter on the Fingertip
ingredients: ½ c (96 g) dry instant oatmeal
¼ tsp (1 g) smooth peanut butter (honey-free)

Sprinkle hemp seeds or another iron-rich seed on top. Scoop the peanut butter Prepare the peanut butter. into a small bowl. Whisk in 1 tsp (5 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps.

Let baby self-feed with the apple oatmeal while you watch for symptom of an allergic reaction to the peanut. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer more tastes of thinned peanut butter.

meals: Bell Pepper Half + Cauliflower Florets + Sesame-Free Hummus + Smooth Peanut Butter

recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) florets + 1 bell pepper half + ½ c (120 ml) hummus

meals: Stewed Pear Half + Textured Rice Porridge with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl

recipes.title: Stewed Pear Half + Textured Rice Porridge with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) porridge + 2 stewed pear halves
ingredients: ¼ c (50 g) dry basmati rice

meals: Chayote or Apple Two Ways with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl

recipes.title: Chayote or Apple Two Ways with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl

meals: Cauliflower Florets + Mashed Edamame

meals: Ginger Peanut Noodles with Broccoli and Tofu + Turnip or Beet Wedges

Quinoa contains insoluble fiber, specifically cellulose, that holds its shape as the food passes through the digestive tract but promotes softer poop and a healthy gut microbiome. Seeing quinoa in poop does not mean that baby did not receive any nutrients; quinoa did its job of helping move along other food in baby’s body.

meals: Coconut Chia Seed Pudding with Peanut Butter Swirl + Mango Two Ways
Plantain Two Ways with Ground-Up Peanut

recipes.title: Coconut Chia Seed Pudding with Peanut Butter Swirl + Mango Two Ways
ingredients: ¾ c (180 ml) coconut chia seed pudding
1 tsp (3 g) hulled unsalted sunflower seeds (optional)
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the leftover pudding from the refrigerator. If you don’t have any, use the directions on Week 8 | Day 54 to prepare more. 2. Scoop the pudding into baby’s bowl. Whisk the peanut butter into the pudding until smooth with no clumps. 3. Wash, dry, peel, and halve the mango. Cut the halves into long, thick spears about the size of two adult fingers pressed together. Set aside 2 to 3 spears for baby’s meal and store the rest for tomorrow. 4. Mash 1 spear, then top it on baby’s pudding. Grind the sunflower seeds into a fine powder, then roll the remaining spears in the powder to add grip.
recipes.howToServe: Place the spears, bowl, and a pre-loaded spoon in front of baby. Let the child self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Chia Seed Pudding keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 1 week. Experiment with Flavor: Chia seeds pack a big punch when it comes to combating hard poop. They are a magnificent source of fiber that not only helps diversify the microbiome, but also helps soften stool. When placed in liquid, chia seeds expand, creating a slimy gel-like texture (mucilage). A little goes a long way so take caution as consuming too much chia seed pudding can make baby feel too full and cause digestive discomfort. For these reasons, offer a small quantity at first and gradually increase the amount over time.

recipes.title: Plantain Two Ways with Ground-Up Peanut
ingredients: ⅓ c (80 ml) unsweetened coconut milk
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash the plantains, then cut off the tips. Cut crosswise into 3 sections—don’t worry about peeling the plantains yet. 2. Bring 4 c (1 liter) of water or stock to a boil, then add the plantains and lower the heat to create a simmer. 3. Cover and cook until the plantains are easily pierced with a knife, between 15 and 30 minutes. Drain. 4. Peel the skins, then cut 3 sections on the diagonal to create discs about the size of 2 adult fingers pressed together. Mash the remaining plantains with the coconut milk until smooth. The mash should be loose and spreadable. If it seems too thick, stir in more coconut milk. Cool until the mixture is barely warm to the touch. 5. Set aside 1 or 2 discs and scoop some mashed plantains into baby’s bowl. Store the rest for tomorrow. Loosen the peanut butter with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of water, then stir the mixture into the mashed plantains.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the plantain discs and the mashed plantain, and let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, pre-load a spoon and rest it next to the bowl for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded spoon or a plantain disc in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked plantains keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. An opened can of coconut milk keeps in an airtight glass container in the fridge for 3 days. Start Big, Then Move Down in Size: Start by offering a large plantain in its whole form or cut into large spears. If baby appears to be managing the size, consider offering a slightly smaller piece to hone baby’s fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Coconut Dal with Rice
recipes.yield: 4 c (1 liter) dal + 3 c (720 ml) rice
recipes.instructions: Prepare the dal. Soak the dal in cold water while you peel and finely chop the garlic and onion. Melt the oil in a pot set on medium-high heat. When the oil shimmers, add the garlic and onion, and stir to coat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft, about 5 minutes. Drain the lentils, then add them to the pot with the coconut milk, spice, and 1 ½ c (360 ml) of fresh water. Bring the pot to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook, partially covered, until the lentils start falling apart, about 10 minutes. Add the cauliflower florets and continue cooking until they are easily pierced with a knife, about 10 minutes. Stir in ghee or butter. Prepare the rice. Rinse the rice, then soak for 30 minutes. Drain. Bring the rice and 1 ¼ c (300 ml) of fresh water to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook until the rice has absorbed the liquid, about 10 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat. Let the rice sit in the pot with the cover on for 5 minutes, then uncover and fluff the rice. Set aside some dal and rice for baby’s meal today and tomorrow. Season your food with salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Mash some dal, rice, and yogurt in baby’s bowl and lay 1 or 2 large cauliflower florets on the side. Let baby self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Coconut Moong Dal and cooked rice keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Leftover Rice? Make Rice Balls: Mashing rice with soft, scoopable foods is one way to get grains in the belly. Rice balls are another: mash 1 tbsp (15 ml) of rice with 2 tsp (10 ml) of dal to form a paste, then roll the mixture into a ball.

meals: Cucumber Strips + Plantain Two Ways with Sesame Tahini Swirl
Lentil and Rice Ball + Labneh or Yogurt Dip + Whole Green Beans

recipes.title: Cucumber Strips + Plantain Two Ways with Sesame Tahini Swirl
recipes.yield: 1-2 plantain discs + ⅓ c (80 ml) mashed plantains + 6-8 cucumber strips
ingredients: ⅓ c (80 ml) cooked mashed sweet plantain
1 tsp (3 g) hulled unsalted sunflower seeds (optional)
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the plantains from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 57 to prepare more. 2. Stir a splash of coconut milk, human milk, formula, and/or water into the mashed plantains to loosen them, then stir in the sesame tahini until the mixture is smooth with no clumps. 3. Wash and peel the cucumber. Cut the cucumber into thin rectangular strips about as thick as your pinky finger. It is okay to keep the seeds and skin on the strips (they get mashed as baby munches) but remove them if they make you nervous. Set aside 1 or 2 cucumber strips for baby’s meal and store the rest. 4. Grind the sunflower seeds into a fine powder, then roll the cucumber strips in the powder to add grip.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the cucumber strips and plantains and let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, pass a piece of food in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked plantains keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Cut cucumber keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Whole cucumber is sensitive to excess moisture when stored in the refrigerator. To help absorb the moisture and extend the life of the vegetable, store it in a bag with a paper towel or kitchen towel to absorb the moisture.

recipes.title: Lentil and Rice Ball + Labneh or Yogurt Dip + Whole Green Beans
ingredients: ¼ c (60 ml) coconut moong dal
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the leftover coconut moong dal and rice from the refrigerator. If you do not have any, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 57 to prepare more or swap the dal for labneh or yogurt to make the rice balls. 2. Mash the dal and rice. Roll 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the mixture between your palms to create a ball. Repeat. If the balls seem too mushy and will mash in baby’s hands, stir in breadcrumbs, chickpea flour, or more cooked rice to bind them. Set aside 2 balls for today’s meal and store the rest for the days ahead.
recipes.howToServe: Stick the whole green beans in the labneh and the lentil-rice balls on the side. Let baby self-feed with the bowl. Show baby how to dip by swiping the green bean in the bowl and passing it in the air to the child.
recipes.howToStore: Lentil and Rice Balls keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. What to Do When Baby Ignores Food: Sometimes baby ignores one food while reaching for another. Stay calm and allow baby to explore, while occasionally reaching in to grab a bite of the ignored food. Your action will gently pique baby’s interest and model how to eat it.

meals: Broccoli Two Ways + Sliced Star Fruit or Pineapple Spears + Salmon Flakes
Cucumber Strips + Lentil and Rice Ball + Tomato Wedge

recipes.title: Broccoli Two Ways + Sliced Star Fruit or Pineapple Spears + Salmon Flakes
recipes.yield: ½ tsp (1 g) fish + 3 c (720 ml) florets
recipes.instructions: 1. Open the can of salmon. Measure ½ tsp (3 ml), which is about equal to half of the length of your pinky finger. Transfer the rest of the fish from the can to an airtight glass container to store for later. Break the salmon into flakes. 2. Wash the broccoli. Cut off the florets from the primary stem. Set aside 1 c (240 ml) of florets to prepare for baby’s meal and store the rest. 3. Place the florets in a steamer basket or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam. 4. Set aside 1 or 2 large florets and mash the rest with the oil until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay. 5. Wash the star fruit. Slice the fruit crosswise to create thin stars about as thick as your pinky finger. Cut off the skin. Remove any seeds.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the large florets and sliced star fruit and let baby touch, grab, and munch. When baby is ready, mash the salmon with some of the mashed broccoli, then offer a pre-loaded spoon to baby. Hold the utensil near baby’s mouth and let the child reach for it. Once baby has grabbed the spoon, let go. Let baby continue to munch on the large florets while you watch for any symptoms of an allergic reaction to the fish. If baby shows no signs after 10 minutes, offer more flaked fish mixed with the mashed florets.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked or canned fish and broccoli keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Model How to Eat: When possible, eat with baby rather than at separate times. The more that we watch baby eat without occupying ourselves with food, the more likely we are to intervene. Research shows heavy fretting and fussing over baby at mealtime is associated with picky eating in toddlerhood and beyond.

recipes.title: Cucumber Strips + Lentil and Rice Ball + Tomato Wedge
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the leftover lentil-rice balls from the refrigerator. If you do not have any, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 58 to prepare more. Or make porridge two ways (Week 1 | Day 4) using instant oatmeal or any grain you have on hand. 2. Grab the cucumber strips from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 58 to prepare more. 3. If you like, grind the sunflower seeds into a fine powder, then roll the cucumber strips in the powder to add grip. 4. Wash, dry, and halve the tomato. Cut one half into 2 to 3 wedges. Store the other half for another use.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the cucumber strips, lentil-rice balls, and tomato wedges and let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, pass a cucumber strip or ball in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cut cucumber and lentil-rice balls keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Windshield Wiper Behavior: Sometimes when baby is overwhelmed by too many food choices, the child pushes away everything in one swoop of the arms and hands. If this happens, consider reducing the number of foods offered at once, bringing out a new food only when baby loses interest in the first one.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Sheet Pan Salmon and Broccoli
recipes.instructions: Assemble the ingredients. Preheat oven to 300 F (149 C). Line a sheet tray with parchment paper. If you start with one large piece of salmon, cut it crosswise to create 3 to 4 fillets, each about 3 in (7 ½ cm) wide. Coat the fish with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of oil. Lay the fish on the tray with the skin side facing down. Peel and quarter the onion. Wash, dry, zest, and juice the lemon. Set the juice aside and toss half of the zest with the onion, broccoli, and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of oil. Evenly space the fish and vegetables on the tray. Bake the fish and vegetables. Bake until a knife inserted into the thickest part of the fish reveals no translucent flesh, about 25 minutes. Use a kitchen thermometer to check that the fish’s internal temperature has reached 145 F (63 C). Remove the tray from the oven. Sprinkle 1 tbsp (15 ml) of lemon juice on the food. Store the rest of the juice for tomorrow. Plate the meal. Mix the remaining oil, zest, labneh, and spice until smooth. Scoop some dip into baby’s bowl. Stick 1 or 2 large florets in baby’s bowl and reserve more florets for baby’s meal tomorrow and the days ahead. Remove the skin from one fillet of fish, then flake the fish for baby. Set aside a scant amount (½ tsp or 1 g) for today’s meal and store the rest. Season the remaining dip, fish, and vegetables for yourself with salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the large florets and let baby touch, grab, and munch. When baby is ready, offer a pre-loaded spoon of fish flakes to baby. Let baby continue to munch on large florets while you watch for any symptoms of an allergic reaction to the fish. If baby shows no signs after a few minutes, offer more flaked fish to baby.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked fish and broccoli keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days.

meals: Avocado Spears + Lentil Rice Ball + Salmon Flakes
Lemony Broccoli Two Ways + Sweet Potato Spears

recipes.title: Avocado Spears + Lentil Rice Ball + Salmon Flakes
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the salmon from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover, open a new can or use the directions on Week 9 | Day 59 to cook a fresh batch. Measure 1 tsp (5 ml) which is about equal in size to your pinky finger. Break the salmon into flakes. 2. Grab the leftover lentil-rice balls from the refrigerator. If you do not have any, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 58 to prepare more. Or make porridge two ways using instant oatmeal or any grain you have on hand. 3. Peel and halve the avocado. Remove the pit and skin. Cut one half into spears and store the other half for later. If you like, grind the sunflower seeds into a fine powder, then roll the avocado spears in the powder to add grip.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the lentil-rice balls and avocado spears, and let baby touch, grab, and munch. When baby is ready, offer a pre-loaded spoon of salmon, then let baby munch on the avocado spears for a few minutes. If all is well, offer more flaked fish.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked fish and lentil-rice balls keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days Adjusting Portion Size: As baby adjust to eating solids, you’ll develop a stronger sense of the child’s eating patterns. Adjust portion sizes to meet the child’s needs and add or omit foods from a menu as needed. Trust your instincts and let baby’s signals tell you if/when they want more or less food.

recipes.title: Lemony Broccoli Two Ways + Sweet Potato Spears
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash, peel, and cut the sweet potato into spears about the size of two adult fingers pressed together. Place the spears in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the spears until they are easily pierced with a knife, about 4 minutes in the microwave and 8 minutes on the stovetop. 2. Grab the florets from the refrigerator. Steam them using the directions on Week 1 | Dayl 1, but keep the florets whole instead of mashing some. 3. Melt the butter. Whisk in the lemon juice. Pour the dressing over the florets. Mash small florets until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay. Scoop some mashed florets into baby’s bowl and sprinkle hemp seeds on top.
recipes.howToServe: Let baby grab, munch, and play with the broccoli florets and sweet potato spears. To get food in the belly, offer a pre-loaded spoon of mashed vegetable and let baby grab it from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked broccoli keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. One Way to Increase Iron: Let baby dip florets and sweet potato spears in hummus or a simple dip made of mashed beans with a small spoonful of lemon juice mixed in. The beans are packed with iron, and the vitamin C in the lemon helps significantly increase iron absorption.

meals: Broccoli Salmon Egg Strips + Raspberry Two Ways
Mashed Edamame with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl + Sweet Potato Spears

recipes.title: Broccoli Salmon Egg Strips + Raspberry Two Ways
recipes.yield: 6-8 egg strips + ¼ c (60 ml) berries
recipes.instructions: Prepare the egg strips. Pull the florets from the refrigerator. Steam them using the directions from Week 1 | Day 1. Set aside the largest floret to serve whole. Finely chop the rest. Crack the eggs into the mixing bowl and add the chopped broccoli, milk, and flaked salmon. Whisk to combine the ingredients. Warm the oil in an 8-inch non-stick skillet set on medium heat. (If you are using a larger skillet, increase the number of eggs so that the mixture covers the bottom of the pan.) When the oil shimmers, pour in the egg mixture and turn the heat to low. Cover and steam until the eggs are firm and the edges have started to curl, about 5 minutes. Transfer the omelet from the pan to a cutting board. Cut into strips about the width of two adult fingers pressed together. Let cool. Prepare the raspberries. Wash the fruit. If the berries are large (about the size of your thumb knuckle) and so soft that they easily mash when gently pressed, keep 1 whole berry to offer to baby as finger food. Otherwise, minimize the choking risk by flattening the berry with your thumb and mashing the rest into a textured purée and swirl the mixture into baby’s labneh.
recipes.howToServe: Offer 1 egg strip and the large broccoli floret with the raspberries and labneh, and let baby try to self-feed. If baby needs help, pass a piece in the air for the child to grab from you. Observe baby for signs of an allergic reaction to the fish. If baby shows no signs, offer another egg strip.
recipes.howToStore: Egg strips and mashed raspberries keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Rashes From Acidic Food: Touching acidic foods like raspberry can cause a contact rash, a harmless skin reaction. This rash often appears near the chin and mouth. If baby is prone to contact rashes, consider applying a barrier ointment (such as petroleum jelly or an oil/wax blend) before mealtime.

recipes.title: Mashed Edamame with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl + Sweet Potato Spears
recipes.instructions: Prepare the edamame. Place the edamame in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the edamame until the beans are soft, about 2 minutes in the microwave or 5 minutes on the stovetop. The edamame is ready when you can easily mash one with a fork. Use a food processor to blend the beans, olive oil, and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water. Add more oil as needed until it reaches a mostly smooth consistency. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole beans or clumps. Scoop half of the mash into baby’s bowl and store the rest for later in the week. Whisk the peanut butter with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of water until smooth, then stir the mixture into the mashed edamame. If the mash seems too thick, add another splash of warm water to thin as desired. Prepare the sweet potatoes. Grab the leftover sweet potato spears from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 9 | Day 60 to prepare more.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the spears and mashed edamame with a pre-loaded spoon on the side for baby to pick up and self-feed. If baby needs help, keep pre-loading the spoon and passing it in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Edamame mash and sweet potato spears keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Mashed edamame can also be stored in the freezer for 2 months. Store it in small portions (a covered ice cube tray or ¼-cup containers) for easy access to baby- friendly portions at mealtime. How to Encourage Utensil Use: If baby isn’t practicing with the spoon yet, try this method. First, pre-load a spoon and pass it in the air for baby to grab. On the next bite, hold the loaded spoon lower down towards the bowl for baby to grab. Finally, set the spoon in the bowl for baby to pick up.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Salmon Cakes
recipes.instructions: Prepare the potato. Wash, peel, and cut the potato into cubes. Add the potato to a pot of water to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook until the potato is easily pierced with a knife, about 10 minutes. Drain. Cool. Mash. Prepare the salmon. Grab the leftover can of salmon from the refrigerator and open two fresh cans. Rinse the fish to remove excess sodium. Flake the fish. Prepare the cakes. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Line a sheet tray with parchment paper. Wash, dry, zest, and juice the lemon. Add half of the zest and 1 tbsp (15 ml) of juice to a mixing bowl and set the rest aside to make the dip. Mash the potatoes, flaked fish, breadcrumbs, eggs, and spices with the lemon juice and zest to form a paste. Shape the mixture into cakes about 2 in (5 cm) in diameter. At this point, salmon cakes can be frozen to cook at a future date. If you plan to cook the cakes right away, evenly space cakes on the tray. Bake until the cakes start to brown on the bottom, about 15 minutes. Flip the cakes and continue to bake 5 more minutes. Prepare the dip. Blend the avocado, labneh, remaining lemon zest, and 1 tbsp (15 ml) lemon juice until smooth. Scoop some dip into baby’s bowl. Season the rest for yourself with salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a salmon cake in the dip so it stands upright, ready for baby to grab. Offer the food to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done. Show baby how to dip by swiping the salmon cake in the dip, and pss the food in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked salmon cakes keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. When freezing, use this trick to keep them from sticking together. First, freeze the cakes on a sheet tray. After they are frozen (about 1 hour later), transfer the cakes to an airtight container to store in the freezer. To defrost, transfer a salmon cake to an airtight container and store in the refrigerator the day before you plan to serve it.

meals: Asparagus Two Ways + Mashed Potato + Salmon Cake
Creamy Cucumber Dip + Spiced Cauliflower Florets

recipes.title: Asparagus Two Ways + Mashed Potato + Salmon Cake
recipes.yield: 1 cake + 1 asparagus spear + 1 c (240 ml) mashed vegetables
recipes.instructions: Prepare the potato. Wash, peel, and cut the potato into cubes. Add the potato to a pot of water to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook until the potato is easily pierced with a knife, about 10 minutes. Drain. Mash the warm potato with 2 tbsp (28 g) butter until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no clumps. Let cool. Prepare the asparagus. Wash the spears and cut off the woody ends. Melt the remaining butter in a skillet. When the butter finishes foaming, add the whole asparagus spears and stir to coat. Add a splash of water and cover the skillet to steam the asparagus. It is ready when easily pierced with a knife but firm enough to hold its shape (not limp) when lifted from the skillet. Set 1 whole spear aside and finely chop the other. Scoop some mashed potatoes into baby’s bowl and fold in the chopped asparagus. Prepare the salmon. Grab a salmon cake from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover, make a fresh batch or offer a broccoli salmon egg strip and toasted bread cut into strips to keep up baby’s exposure to both finned fish and wheat.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the salmon cake, whole asparagus spear, and mashed vegetables to baby and let the child self-feed. If baby needs help, pass the whole asparagus spear or salmon cake in the air for the child to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked salmon cakes, asparagus, and potato keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Prioritize Your Goals: Folding finely chopped asparagus helps get food in the belly, while a whole asparagus spear helps baby build a mental map of the mouth as the child moves the tongue around the spear and mashes it with the gums. Either option is a good one.

recipes.title: Creamy Cucumber Dip + Spiced Cauliflower Florets
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) dip + 3 c (720 ml) florets
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cauliflower. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Wash the cauliflower. Cut off the florets from the primary stem. Wash, dry, zest, and juice the lemon. Coat the cauliflower in 2 tbsp (30 ml) of oil, the lemon zest, and the spice. Evenly space the florets on a sheet tray. Roast until the florets starts to brown and a knife easily inserts into the thickest stalk, about 20 minutes. Remove the tray from the oven and set aside some large florets for baby’s meal and season with a small drizzle of lemon juice. Season your florets with lemon juice and salt to taste. Prepare the dip. Shred the cucumber. Whisk the labneh, remaining 2 tbsp (30 ml) of oil, 1 tbsp (15 ml) of lemon juice, and the mint (finely chopped) until smooth. Fold in the shredded cucumber. Scoop some dip into baby’s bowl. If you are planning to eat alongside baby, season some dip for yourself with salt to taste. Grind sesame seeds into a fine powder, then sprinkle the powder over the dip.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a large floret in the dip and offer the rest alongside the dip and let baby self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked cauliflower and creamy cucumber dip keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days Spice as You Like: It’s okay to introduce your favorite spices as soon as baby is ready to start solids, and in fact, it can help minimize picky eating in toddlerhood and beyond. Research shows that babies and toddlers learn to love what they eat early and often.

meals: Asparagus Two Ways + Broccoli Salmon Egg Strip
Mashed Edamame with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl and Raspberry

recipes.title: Mashed Edamame with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl and Raspberry

meals: Coconut Porridge with Sesame Tahini Swirl + Papaya Two Ways
Cucumber Strips + Sesame Hummus

recipes.title: Coconut Porridge with Sesame Tahini Swirl + Papaya Two Ways
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) porridge + 1 mango pit + 4-6 mango spears
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) unsweetened coconut milk
recipes.instructions: 1. Bring the milk and ¼ c (60 ml) of water to a boil. Slowly pour the buckwheat cereal into the boiling milk and water, whisking as you pour. 2. Lower the heat and cook the porridge, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, for 10 minutes. 3. Turn off the heat, stir in the cinnamon, and let the porridge rest in the pot with the cover off for 5 minutes. 4. Scoop the porridge into baby’s bowl. Swirl in the 5. Peel and cut the papaya into handles about the width of two adult fingers pressed together. Set aside 3 handles to serve today and store the rest. Cut 1 handle into bite-sized pieces about the size of your knuckle.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the porridge and papaya and let baby self-feed. If help is needed, pass a papaya handle or a spoon pre-loaded with porridge in the air for baby to grab from you. Refrain from sticking bite-sized pieces of papaya in baby’s mouth.
recipes.howToStore: Porridge keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Cut papaya keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. An opened can of coconut milk keeps in an airtight glass container in the fridge for 3 days. When to Move Down in Size: Baby may not be able to pick up bite-sized pieces of food yet, but the practice helps advance the pincer grasp, which develops around this age. If the small size makes you nervous, it’s okay to wait until you feel baby is ready.

recipes.title: Cucumber Strips + Sesame Hummus
recipes.yield: 2 c (480 ml) hummus + 2 cucumber strips + 6-8 cucumber slices
ingredients: 1 tsp (3 g) hulled unsalted sunflower seeds (optional)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the hummus. Rinse the chickpeas. Halve and juice the lemon. Blend the chickpeas, lemon juice, olive oil, sesame tahini, and spice until mostly smooth. A little texture is okay, but if the hummus is too thick, add a splash or two of water and continue to blend until it reaches the desired consistency. A high-powered food processor speeds up this task, but if you don’t have one, make a chickpea mash by smashing and mixing the ingredients until there are no whole chickpeas. Scoop some hummus into baby’s bowl and store the rest for the days ahead. Prepare the cucumber. Wash and peel the cucumber. Cut the cucumber into thin rectangular strips about the thickness of your pinky finger. It is okay to keep the seeds and skin on the cucumber; they get mashed as baby munches but remove them if they make you nervous. Set aside 1 or 2 strips for baby’s meal and store the rest. If you like, grind the sunflower seeds into a fine powder, then roll the cucumber strips in the powder to add grip.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a cucumber strip in baby’s hummus and offer the bowl with the rest on the side. Let baby grab and munch the cucumber strips and dip cucumber strips and fingers in the hummus. If baby needs help picking up the slices, pass one in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Sesame Hummus and cut cucumber keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Consider the Cucumber Skin: Try offering cucumber with the skin on to build familiarity with texture and promote chewing skills. Cucumber skin may lead to less food in the belly (baby may spit it out) but munching the texture strengthens the gums.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Caprese Salad
recipes.instructions: Prepare the basil oil. Wash and dry the basil. Blend the basil and oil until smooth. A small food processor speeds up this task. If you don’t have a food processor, use a mortar and pestle to smash it, or a knife to finely chop it, then whisk the basil and oil in a mixing bowl. With this method, flecks of basil are okay as long as there are no large pieces of leaf. Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to combine flavors. Assemble the salad. Wash, dry, and cut the tomato into a mix of wedges and bite-sized pieces. Cut the mozzarella into thin round slices. Drizzle the tomato and mozzarella with basil oil. Set aside some Caprese for baby, then season your portion with balsamic vinegar and salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the Caprese to baby and let the child self-feed. Let baby try to pick up the bite-sized pieces of tomato, and if they need help, pass a bite-sized piece of food in the air for the child to grab from you. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Caprese keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Sensory Play With Plants: Set aside one of the largest basil leaves to share with baby as part of the meal. The child will likely not consume the leaf, but they’ll benefit from invaluable sensory play by touching, smelling, and tasting the bold flavor.

meals: Edamame Mash with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl + Tomato Wedge
Creamy Cucumber Dip + Sardine Two Ways
familyMeal: Asparagus and Potato Salad with Egg and Ricotta

recipes.title: Edamame Mash with Smooth Peanut Butter Swirl + Tomato Wedge
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) edamame mash + 6-8 tomato wedges
recipes.instructions: Prepare the edamame. Place the edamame in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the edamame until the beans are soft, about 2 minutes in the microwave or 5 minutes on the stovetop. The edamame is ready when you can easily mash one with a fork. Use a food processor to blend the edamame, oil, and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water. Add more oil as needed until it reaches a mostly smooth consistency. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole beans or clumps. Scoop some mash into baby’s bowl and store the rest for later. Whisk the peanut butter with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of water until smooth, then stir the mixture into the mashed edamame in baby’s bowl. Prepare the tomato. Wash, dry, and halve the tomato. Cut one half into 2 to 3 wedges. Store the other half for another use.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the tomato wedge and the mashed edamame with a pre-loaded spoon nestled on the side for baby to grab. Let the child self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Edamame mash and cut tomato keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. When freezing edamame, store it in small portions (a covered ice cube tray or ¼-cup containers) for up to 2 months. This way, you have easy access to baby-friendly portions at mealtime.

recipes.title: Creamy Cucumber Dip + Sardine Two Ways
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) dip + 2-3 toast strips + ½ c (120 ml) sardine salad + 1 sandwich
recipes.instructions: Prepare the dip. Cut the cucumber into spears (keep the skin on or peel it if you prefer), then shred 1 spear and store the rest for the week ahead. Wash, dry, zest, and juice the lemon. Whisk the zest and 1 tsp (5 ml) of lemon juice with⅓ c (80 ml) of yogurt, the oil, and the mint (finely chopped) until smooth. Fold in the shredded cucumber. Prepare the sardines. Open the tin and remove the fish. Rinse the fish to remove excess sodium. The tiny bones are edible and full of nutrition but remove them if they make you nervous. Set aside 1 fish to serve whole. Mash the remaining fish with the remaining yogurt, 1 tsp (5 ml) of lemon juice, and the spices. Set aside a scoop or two of fish salad for baby and season the rest for yourself with salt to taste. Toast the bread until lightly browned, then cut 1 slice into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together for baby. Spread a thin layer of sardine salad on the bread. Season the rest for yourself with salt to taste and make yourself a sandwich.
recipes.howToServe: Lay the whole sardine fillet on the side of baby’s cucumber dip, then offer the bowl and the toast strips and let baby self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Cut cucumber and creamy cucumber dip keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Canned sardines, once opened, don’t last long in the refrigerator—eat within a day or two. Edible Bones in Tiny Tinned Fish: Even a can of “boneless” sardines may contain tiny pin bones. The canning process softens these bones, which makes them edible and safe for babies and toddlers to eat, but if the bones make you nervous, pick them out before serving.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Asparagus and Potato Salad with Egg and Ricotta
ingredients: 1 ½ c (360 ml) fresh ricotta cheese
2 tbsp (30 ml) unsalted butter nutrients, age-appropriate sizes, and more:
recipes.instructions: Prepare the eggs and potatoes. Bring a pot of water to boil. Lower the heat to create a simmer, then gently lower each egg into the pot. Add the potatoes. Cover the pot and cook for 12 minutes, then lift the eggs from the pot to a bowl of ice water. Keep cooking the potatoes until they are easily pierced with a knife, about 8 minutes more. Drain. Cut the potatoes into quarters while they are warm but cool enough to handle. Set aside some quarters for baby and place the rest in a mixing bowl. Prepare the dressing and cheese. Zest and juice the lemon. Whisk the zest into the ricotta and set aside to let the lemon infuse the cheese. Next, whisk the oil and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of lemon juice. Pour half of the dressing over the warm potatoes. Prepare the asparagus. Wash the spears. Keep 3 whole spears for baby and cut the rest into 1-inch slices. Add the asparagus spears and ½ c (120 ml) of water to a skillet. Cover and steam the asparagus until easily pierced with a fork but firm enough to hold its shape (not limp) when lifted from the skillet. Set 1 whole spear aside and store the other 2 spears for tomorrow. Toss the chopped asparagus with the remaining dressing. Assemble the salad. Spread some lemony ricotta cheese in the bottom of your bowl and baby’s bowl. Top with some asparagus, potatoes, and eggs: finely chopped eggs for baby and halved eggs for yourself. Sprinkle your portion with salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the bowl to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: The salad keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days.

meals: Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal + Smooth Almond Butter on the Fingertip
Asparagus Spear Two Ways + Mashed Potatoes + Tomato Wedges

recipes.title: Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal + Smooth Almond Butter on the Fingertip
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) oatmeal + 2 apple halves
ingredients: ¼ c (48 g) dry instant oatmeal
¼ tsp (1 g) smooth almond butter (honey-free)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the apple. Wash, peel, and halve the apple. Remove the core, seeds, and stem. Place the apple halves in a small pot. Add 1 c (240 ml) of water. Cover and set the pot on medium-high heat. As soon as the water begins boiling, lower the heat to create a steady simmer. Cook until the apple is easily pierced with a fork, about 10 minutes. Remove the apple halves from the pot. Prepare the oatmeal. Measure ½ c (120 ml) of the apple stewing water and discard the rest. Bring the water to a boil, then pour it into the oatmeal. Add the cinnamon. Cook, stirring frequently, until the oats thicken, about 2 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture sit until thickened and cooled, about 10 minutes. Scoop a heaping spoonful (about 2 tbsp / 30 ml) of oatmeal and form it into a ball. If the oatmeal is too loose to form a ball, add a spoonful or two of instant oats to thicken the mixture. Mash 1 stewed apple half into the rest of the oatmeal. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top. Prepare the almond butter. Scoop the almond butter into a small bowl. Whisk in 1 tsp (5 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps.
recipes.howToServe: Let baby munch on the oatmeal ball. After a few minutes, introduce the thinned almond butter: dip your finger in the thinned almond butter, then offer your finger to baby. Let baby taste the flavor, then repeat once or twice to get adequate exposure to the tree nut. Offer the apple oatmeal and let baby self-feed while you watch for signs of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer more tastes of the almond butter.
recipes.howToStore: Oatmeal keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. If oatmeal contains human milk, use it within 4 days. Spice it Up: Switch up the spices! Instead of cinnamon, try using allspice or nutmeg for some warmth and sweetness.

recipes.title: Asparagus Spear Two Ways + Mashed Potatoes + Tomato Wedges
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) mashed potato + 1 asparagus spear + 3-4 tomato wedges
recipes.instructions: Prepare the potato. Wash, peel, and cut the potatoes into cubes. Add the potato to a pot of water to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook until the potato is easily pierced with a knife, about 10 minutes. Drain. Cool. Mash with the oil. Scoop half of the potatoes into baby’s bowl and store the rest for tomorrow. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top. Prepare the asparagus. Grab the cooked asparagus spears from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover, prepare more using the directions from yesterday’s family meal. Set aside one whole spear to serve whole. Finely chop the other. Scoop some mashed potatoes into baby’s bowl and fold in the chopped asparagus. Prepare the tomato. Grab the leftover tomato half from the refrigerator. Cut the tomato into 2 to 3 wedges. Set aside 1 or 2 wedges for today’s meal and store the rest for tomorrow.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the whole asparagus spear, tomato wedge, and the mashed vegetables to baby and let the child self-feed. If baby needs help, pass the whole asparagus spear in the air for the child to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked asparagus, cut tomato, and mashed potatoes keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. One Way to Boost Iron: Have some leftover beans, mashed edamame, or tofu from another meal? Serve it with this meal, which is packed with vitamin C to help baby’s body absorb the plant-based iron in the legumes. See more iron-rich food ideas.

meals: Coconut Porridge with Smooth Almond Butter Swirl + Mango Pit

recipes.title: Coconut Porridge with Smooth Almond Butter Swirl + Mango Pit
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) porridge + 1 mango pit + ¼ c (60 ml) bite-sized mango pieces
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) unsweetened coconut milk
½ tsp (3 g) smooth almond butter (honey-free)
recipes.instructions: 1. Place the instant oats in baby’s bowl. 2. Bring the coconut milk and ¼ c (60 ml) of water to a boil, then pour it into the bowl. Stir to combine the oats and water. Let the mixture sit until thickened and cooled, about 10 minutes. 3. Scoop a heaping spoonful (about 2 tbsp / 30 ml) of oatmeal and form it into a ball. If the oatmeal is too loose to form a ball, add a spoonful or two of instant oats to thicken the mixture. 4. Scoop the almond butter into a small bowl. Whisk in 2 tsp (10 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps. Swirl the thinned almond butter into baby’s oatmeal. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top. 5. Grab the mango pit and spears from the refrigerator. Cut the spears into bite-sized pieces (about the size of your knuckle). Roll the bite-sized pieces in coconut flakes.
recipes.howToServe: Start by letting baby munch on the mango pit and oatmeal ball. After a few minutes, offer the almond: pass baby a pre-loaded spoon of oatmeal with the thinned almond butter mixed in. Repeat once or twice so the child gets exposure to almond. Let baby play with and try to pick up the bite-sized mango pieces while you watch for signs of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after a few minutes, offer more oatmeal.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked oatmeal keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days.

recipes.title: Cucumber Strips + Mashed Potatoes + Tomato Wedge
recipes.yield: 2 cucumber strips + ½ c (120 ml) mashed potatoes + 2 tomato wedges
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the mashed potatoes from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover, use the directions from Week 10 / Day 66 / Meal 2 to prepare more. Stir 1 tbsp (15 ml) of warm water, human milk, and/ or formula into the potatoes to loosen the mixture. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top. 2. Grab the leftover cucumber strips and tomato wedges from the refrigerator.
recipes.howToServe: Offer cucumber strips, tomato wedges, and mashed potatoes with a pre-loaded spoon and let baby self-feed. One Way to Boost Iron: Have some leftover beans, mashed edamame, or tofu from another meal? Serve it with this meal, which is packed with vitamin C to help baby’s body absorb the plant-based iron in the legumes. See more iron-rich food ideas.

meals: Pumpkin Almond Pancake with Peanut-Sesame Drizzle and Raspberries
Lemony Sardine Penne
familyMeal: Lamb Meatballs and Winter Squash with Yogurt Sauce

recipes.title: Pumpkin Almond Pancake with Peanut-Sesame Drizzle and Raspberries
recipes.instructions: Prepare the batter. Peel and mash the banana. Whisk all ingredients except the vinegar, baking soda, oil, peanut butter, and tahini in a bowl until no streaks of flour remain. Whisk the baking soda and vinegar in a separate bowl, then pour into the batter. Whisk to combine. Cook the pancakes. Warm the oil in a non-stick skillet set on medium heat. Once it shimmers, swirl to coat the skillet, then add spoonfuls of batter, using the back of the spoon to gently flatten each scoop into a pancake. Cook until the bottoms are golden, about 3 minutes. Flip, then cook to brown the other side, about 2 minutes more. Transfer to a plate. Repeat until all batter is used. If the pancakes are large, cut one into bite-sized pieces or strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together for baby. If the pancakes are small, offer them whole. Prepare the drizzle. Whisk the peanut butter and sesame tahini with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps. Prepare the raspberries. Wash the fruit. If the berries are large (about the size of your thumb knuckle) and so soft that they easily mash when gently pressed, keep the berries whole for baby to practice picking up. Otherwise, minimize the choking risk by flattening the berries with your finger or mashing the berries into a textured purée.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the raspberries and pancake with a spoonful of the thinned peanut-sesame drizzle on top. Let baby self-feed. If help is needed, pass the pancake in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Pumpkin Almond Pancakes keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days or in the freezer for 2 months. To keep pancakes from sticking in the freezer, allow them to cool, lay in a single layer on a pan, then freeze. Once the pancakes are completely frozen (after about 30 minutes), transfer them to an airtight container to store in the freezer. Best Pancake Sizes for Baby: The goal is for baby to hold the food on their own. If pancakes are small (under 3 inches or 7 ½ cm in diameter), serve them whole. Cut larger pancakes into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together or in bite-sized pieces to hone the pincer grasp.

recipes.title: Lemony Sardine Penne
recipes.instructions: Prepare the breadcrumbs. Melt 1 tbsp (14 g) of butter in a large skillet set on medium heat. Stir in the breadcrumbs and toast to your liking, then transfer them to a bowl. Zest and juice the lemon. Finely chop the basil. Mix the zest and basil into the breadcrumbs. Prepare the sauce. Set a large pot of water on high heat. As it warms, open the sardines and rinse the fish. Separate each fish into two fillets. Remove any bones if you like, though they are edible, soft, and safe for baby to eat. Next, peel and finely chop the shallot and garlic. Warm the remaining butter over medium heat in the same skillet used to toast the breadcrumbs (no need to wash it). Add the shallot and garlic and cook until the shallot has softened, about 5 minutes, then stir in the sardines. Decrease the heat to the lowest setting to keep the mixture warm. Cook the penne. Cook the penne in the boiling water until soft (not al dente), about 10 minutes. Use a sieve or slotted spoon to lift the pasta directly from the pot to the skillet with the sardines. Add ⅓ c (80 ml) of pasta cooking water, 1 tbsp (15 ml) of lemon juice, and half the breadcrumb mixture to the skillet. Stir to coat. Set aside some penne and a sardine for baby. Season your portion with parmesan cheese, more lemon juice, black pepper, and salt to taste. Sprinkle the breadcrumb mixture on top.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the penne and sardine to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Lemony Sardine Penne keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days. Lentil Penne and Other Iron-Fortified Pastas: If you want to boost iron in baby’s diet, try pasta made with chickpeas and lentils, which are higher in iron than wheat-based pasta. There are also lots of brands that fortify wheat-based pasta with iron.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Lamb Meatballs and Winter Squash with Yogurt Sauce
recipes.yield: 10-12 meatballs + 16-20 squash handles + 1 ¾ c (420 ml) dip
ingredients: 1 ½ c (360 ml) plain yogurt nutrients, age-appropriate sizes, and more:
recipes.instructions: Prepare the meatballs. Defrost frozen meat in the refrigerator the day before you plan to cook. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Line a sheet tray with parchment. Peel the garlic and onion. Smash 1 clove and set aside. Finely chop the other clove and the onion. Mash and mix the meat, chopped garlic and onion, egg, almond flour, spice, and herb. Shape the mixture into 2-inch-wide meatballs. Evenly space the meatballs on the tray. Prepare the squash. Line a second sheet tray with parchment paper. Halve the acorn squash. Scoop out the seeds. Cut the halves into 1-inch handles. Coat the squash with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of oil. Evenly space the squash handles on the tray. Cook the meatballs and squash. Roast for 20 minutes, then check the food. It is ready when the squash is easily pierced with a fork and no pink meat remains in the center of a meatball when cut open. If you like, use a food thermometer to check that the meat’s internal temperature has reached 145 F (63 C). Set aside food for baby’s meal today and tomorrow. Peel the skins and mash baby’s acorn squash handles. Season your food with salt to taste and keep it warm while baby’s food cools.
recipes.howToServe: Offer 1 meatball and some mashed squash with sauce drizzled on top. Let baby self-feed. Eat alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Lamb meatballs and cooked acorn squash keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Double the Batch: Meatballs freeze exceptionally well. If you like the recipe and cook it again, consider making double the amount and freezing extras for a future dinner. Just defrost in the refrigerator the day before you want to reheat them.

meals: Bulgur Squash Mash + Lamb Meatball

recipes.title: Bulgur Squash Mash + Lamb Meatball
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) bulgur + ½ c (120 ml) squash + 1 meatball
ingredients: ¼ c (60 ml) mashed acorn squash
recipes.instructions: 1. Bring the bulgur and 1 c (240 ml) of water or stock to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cover and cook until the liquid is fully absorbed, about 12 minutes. Drain any excess water, then fluff the grains. 2. Grab the meatball and squash from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on 3. Measure ¼ c (60 ml) of cooked bulgur and store the rest for later today. Mash the bulgur and squash. Let cool. 4. Scoop the mash into baby’s bowl, dollop the yogurt on the side, and top with the meatball.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the bowl to baby and let the child self-feed. If baby needs help, pre-load a spoon and rest it next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded utensil in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked acorn squash, bulgur, and meatballs keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Play with Flavor: Try cooking bulgur and other grains and pastas in meat stock, which not only adds flavor but essential nutrients like iron.

recipes.title: Bulgur Ball + Edamame and Garden Pea Mash
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the bulgur from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 10 | Day 69 | Meal 1 to prepare more. 2. Wash and dry the herbs and lemon. Finely chop the leaves. Zest and juice the lemon. Set aside. 3. Place the edamame and garden peas in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam until the beans are soft, about 2 minutes in the microwave or 5 minutes on the stovetop. They are ready when the edamame can be easily mashed with a fork. 4. Use a food processor to blend the edamame and peas with the oil, chopped herbs, lemon zest, 1 tbsp (15 ml) of lemon juice, and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water. Add more oil as needed until it reaches a mostly smooth consistency. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole beans or clumps. 5. Scoop some mash into baby’s bowl and store the rest for later. Scoop 1 tbsp (15 ml) of mash from baby’s bowl and mix it with the bulgur to form a paste. Wet your hands, scoop half the paste, and roll it between your palms to create a ball, then repeat to create a second ball. If the ball crumbles easily, add more edamame-garden pea mash to thicken the paste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the bulgur ball and edamame-pea mash and let baby self-feed. To encourage the use of a utensil, pre-load a spoon and rest it next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded spoon in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked bulgur, edamame, and garden peas keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months.

meals: Edamame-Garden Pea Dip + Salmon Cake
Pinto Beans Two Ways + Steamed Corn Cob + Tomato Two Ways

recipes.title: Edamame-Garden Pea Dip + Salmon Cake
ingredients: ¼ c (60 ml) edamame- garden pea mash
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the salmon cake from the freezer and defrost in the microwave or oven. If you do not have any leftover, use the directions from Week 9 | Day 61 | Family Meal to prepare more. Alternatively, swap the salmon cake for sardines to keep up baby’s exposure to finned fish, and use the sardines two ways from baby. 2. Prepare the dip by whisking the yogurt and almond butter into the leftover edamame-garden pea mash until smooth. A little texture is okay as long as there are no clumps of almond butter. If you do not have leftover mash, use the directions from Week 10 | Day 69 | Meal 2 to prepare more.
recipes.howToServe: Stick the salmon cake in the dip so it is ready for baby to grab. Offer the food and let baby self- feed. If help is needed, pre-load a spoon and rest it next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded spoon in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked salmon cakes keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Edamame-garden pea dip keeps in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days.

recipes.title: Pinto Beans Two Ways + Steamed Corn Cob + Tomato Two Ways
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) beans + 1 corn cob + tomato wedges
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) cooked pinto beans
recipes.instructions: Prepare the corn. Peel and shuck the corn husk and silk. Cut off the stem and tip, then cut the cob into 2 or 3 rounds about the width of three adult fingers pressed together. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the corn cob rounds and boil until the corn has brightened in color and softened slightly, about 8 minutes. Drain. Run cold water over the corn cob rounds to cool them down for baby. Prepare the beans. Rinse the beans. Set aside a few beans to serve whole and minimize the risk by flattening them with your thumb. Mash the remaining beans with the yogurt until mostly smooth. Prepare the tomato. Wash, dry, and halve the tomato. Cut one half into 2 to 3 wedges, then cut 1 wedge into bite-sized pieces (about the size of your knuckle). Store the other half for another use.
recipes.howToServe: Place the corn cob rounds with the beans and tomatoes two ways in front of baby and let the child self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked corn on the cob, beans, and cut tomato keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. The beans can also be stored in the freezer for 2 months. How to Safely Offer Whole Pinto Beans: Cooked beans like pinto beans, while roundish in shape, are not a common choking hazard. However, the best thing you can do to prevent choking—with all foods—is to create a safe eating environment, fastening baby in an upright highchair, and staying within arm’s reach at all times.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Almond Pancake with Peanut-Sesame Drizzle
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab a pancake from the freezer. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 10 | Day 68 | Meal 1 to prepare more. 2. Reheat the pancake in the microwave, oven, or toaster. 3. If the pancake is small, offer it whole. If the pancake is large, cut it into bite-sized pieces to promote the pincer grasp or strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together if baby is not ready to pick up smaller pieces of food. 4. Whisk the sesame tahini and peanut butter with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the pancake and sauce and let baby self-feed. If help is needed, pass the pancake in the air for baby to grab from you. If baby seems hesitant to bring to the food to the mouth, model how it’s done by eating a pancake alongside baby. Show baby how to dip the pancake in the sauce and paint on the plate or tray.
