While the oil is warming, peel and finely chop the onions and garlic. When the oil shimmers, add the onion and garlic and stir to coat. Cook until the onion has softened, about 5 minutes. Add the meat to the onions. Break up the meat into crumbles, then stir to coat crumbles in the oil and onion. Cook until the meat is browned, about 15 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste. Cook until the tomato paste starts to brown, about 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes and bay leaves, then bring the mixture to a lively simmer. Cook, partially covered, until the sauce starts to thicken, about 45 minutes. For an extra-thick sauce, cook uncovered until desired consistency is reached. Cook the penne. Set a large pot of water on high heat. Add the penne when the water boils and cook until soft (not al dente), about 10 minutes. Drain. Toss the pasta with some of the sauce, then store the rest of the sauce for tomorrow. Set aside some penne and sauce for baby. Season your portion with salt to taste and sprinkle parmesan cheese on top before serving. Keep your pasta warm while baby’s pasta cools to room temperature.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the pasta to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat your portion alongside baby to model how it’s done. To encourage the use of a utensil, pierce a piece of penne with an age-appropriate fork, then rest the utensil next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded fork in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Bolognese sauce keeps in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Avoid Cracked Containers in the Freezer: Let the sauce cool in airtight containers on the countertop for 30 minutes, then transfer the containers to the refrigerator to cool overnight. The next day, transfer the jars to the freezer. When freezing sauces and soups, take care to leave some space at the top of the container so that the sauce can expand as it solidifies.

meals: Carrot Two Ways + Hummus
Penne Pasta with Bolognese Sauce

recipes.title: Carrot Two Ways + Hummus
recipes.yield: ⅓ c (80 ml) carrot + ½ c (120 ml) hummus
recipes.instructions: Prepare the carrot. Wash, dry, and peel the carrots. Halve the carrots lengthwise, then cut the halves crosswise into sticks about the length of your pointer finger. Place the carrot sticks in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the carrot sticks until they have softened slightly, but hold together when pressed, about 4 minutes in the microwave or 8 minutes on the stovetop. Set aside 4 to 6 carrot sticks to serve whole today and tomorrow. Mash the rest with the oil. Prepare the hummus. Grab the hummus from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 12 | Day 78 | Meal 2 to prepare more. Mix ¼ c (60 ml) of mashed carrot with the hummus and store the rest of the mashed carrot for tomorrow. If the carrot hummus seems very thick, stir in a splash of warm water to loosen it.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a steamed carrot stick in baby’s hummus and offer the bowl with a pre-loaded spoon of hummus and 2 to 3 carrot sticks on the side. Let baby grab and munch the food and dip fingers in the hummus. If baby needs help picking up the carrot sticks, pass one in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked carrot sticks and hummus keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. When to Serve Baby Carrots: Cooked baby carrots can be mashed for babies under 12 months of age, but it is best to wait until the toddler years to offer baby carrots in their whole form (either raw or cooked) due to the high choking risk. See Carrot in the First Foods® database for more details.

recipes.title: Penne Pasta with Bolognese Sauce
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) pasta + ½ c (120 ml) sauce
recipes.instructions: Prepare the sauce. Grab the sauce from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 12 | Day 78 | Family Meal to prepare more. Cook the penne. Set a small pot of water on high heat. When it boils, cook the penne in the boiling water until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain. Toss the pasta and sauce. Cool to room temperature.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the pasta to baby and let the child self-feed. To encourage the use of a utensil, pierce a piece of penne with an age-appropriate fork, then rest the utensil next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded fork in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Bolognese sauce keeps in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Iron-Rich Pasta: If you want to boost iron in baby’s diet, try pasta made with chickpeas and lentils, which are higher in iron than wheat-based pasta. Lots of brands also fortify wheat-based pasta with iron.

meals: Carrot Two Ways with Ground-Up Walnut
Cauliflower Florets + Herby Avocado Dip

recipes.title: Carrot Two Ways with Ground-Up Walnut
recipes.instructions: Prepare the carrots. Grab the carrots from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 12 | Day 79 | Meal 1 to prepare more. Roll the carrot sticks in hemp seeds. Prepare the walnut. Grind the walnut into a coarse meal, ensuring the texture is consistent with no hard nut pieces remaining. When introducing a new tree nut, grind a cup of the nut to the appropriate consistency and store in a jar in the refrigerator or freezer. This way, you have easy access to the ingredient at mealtime.
recipes.howToServe: Start the meal by letting baby munch on the steamed carrot sticks and scoop the mashed carrot. After a few minutes, introduce ground-up walnut: wet your finger then dip it in the walnut meal and offer your finger to baby. Let baby taste the flavor, then repeat once or twice, so the child gets exposure to walnut. Let baby continue to self-feed on the carrots while you watch for signs of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer more tastes of the walnut.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked carrot sticks and hummus keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. A Boost of Iron: If you would like to round out this meal and boost iron, add a protein on the side, such as bean patties, ground lamb, or smashed chickpeas—your choice. See more iron-rich food ideas.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Florets + Herby Avocado Dip
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) cauliflower + ½ c (120 ml) dip
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cauliflower. Wash the cauliflower. Cut off the florets from the primary stem. Set aside 1 c (240 ml) of florets to prepare for baby’s meal and store the rest for later. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the florets. Season the florets with oil. Let cool. Prepare the dip. Halve the avocado. Peel and mash one half. Store the other half for another use. Halve and juice the lime. Stir 1 tsp (5 ml) into the mashed avocado. Store the rest for another use. Wash, dry, and finely chop the cilantro leaves and delicate stems. Stir the herb into the mashed avocado. Sprinkle hemp seeds on top.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a large floret in the herby avocado dip and offer the bowl with more large florets on the side. Let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, show the child how to dip: swipe the floret in the dip, then pass the floret in the air for baby to touch, grab, and munch.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked cauliflower keeps an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Start Early with Seasonings: Babies learn to like what they eat from the very beginning. If you want your toddler to enjoy herbs and spices, start offering seasonings now so baby builds familiarity with flavors and textures.

meals: Coconut Porridge with Ground-Up Walnut + Pear Two Ways
Bolognese Sauce + Zucchini Spears

recipes.title: Coconut Porridge with Ground-Up Walnut + Pear Two Ways
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) unsweetened coconut milk
recipes.instructions: 1. Bring the coconut milk and ¼ c (60 ml) of water to a boil. Slowly pour the oatmeal into the boiling water, whisking as you pour. 2. Lower the heat and cook the porridge, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, for 2 minutes. 3. Turn off the heat, stir in the cinnamon, and let the porridge rest in the pot with the cover off for 5 minutes. walnut into a consistent coarse meal, ensuring all hard pieces are well-ground, then sprinkle ½ tsp (2 ½ ml) on top. Let cool. 5. Wash the pear. You can keep the skin on or peel it. Halve, core, and slice the pear into quarters lengthwise. Cut 2 quarters into ruler-thin slices. If the pear is very ripe, cut the other 2 quarters into bite-sized pieces (about the size of your knuckle).
recipes.howToServe: Offer the porridge and pear two ways and let baby self-feed. Watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction to walnut. If baby seems okay after a few minutes, sprinkle the rest of the ground walnut on top of baby’s food.
recipes.howToStore: Porridge keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Cut pear keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. An opened can of coconut milk keeps in an airtight glass container in the fridge for 3 days. Consider the Pear Skin: Try offering pear with the skin on to build familiarity with texture and promote chewing skills. Pear skin may lead to less food in the belly (baby may spit it out) but munching the texture strengthens the gums.

recipes.title: Bolognese Sauce + Zucchini Spears
recipes.instructions: Prepare the sauce. Grab the bolognese sauce from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions from Week 12 | Day 78 | Family Meal to prepare more. Prepare the zucchini. Wash the zucchini. Cut off and discard the stem and flower ends. Halve the zucchini lengthwise, then cut each half lengthwise to create spears. If the spears are very long, cut them in half or in thirds to make them the length of an adult pointer finger. Place the spears in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the spears until they have brightened in color and softened slightly, but hold together when pressed, about 3 minutes in the microwave or 6 minutes on the stovetop.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a zucchini spear in the sauce and offer the bowl with more spears on the side. Let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, show the child how to dip: swipe the spear in the sauce, then pass the spear in the air for baby to touch, grab, and munch.
recipes.howToStore: Bolognese sauce and zucchini spears keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. More Ways to Offer Bolognese Sauce: There are lots of ways to serve this iron-rich sauce to baby. Some ideas: mash it with breadcrumbs, millet, or rice and form the paste into balls. Use it as a topping for polenta (corn grits). Mix it into mashed vegetables. Or spread the sauce on toast.

meals: Apple Nut Pancake with Thinned Nut Butter Drizzle
Edamame Mash + Orange

recipes.title: Apple Nut Pancake with Thinned Nut Butter Drizzle
ingredients: ½ tsp (3 g) smooth cashew butter (honey-free)
½ tsp (3 g) smooth peanut butter (honey-free)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the batter. Blend the egg, applesauce, milk, vanilla extract, and walnuts in a blender until smooth. Add the flours, baking powder, and spice. Pulse to combine. Cook the pancakes. Warm half of the butter in a non-stick skillet set on medium heat. Once the butter finishes foaming, swirl to coat the skillet, then add spoonfuls of batter, using the back of the spoon to gently flatten each scoop into a pancake. Cook until the bottoms are golden, about 3 minutes. Flip, then cook to brown the other side, about 2 minutes more. Transfer to a plate. Repeat until all batter is used and add more butter as needed to keep the pancakes from sticking. If the pancakes are large, cut one into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together for baby. If the pancakes are small, set aside one to offer whole. Store the rest. Prepare the drizzle. Whisk the cashew butter, peanut butter, and sesame tahini with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the pancake topped with a drizzle of thinned nut and seed butter sauce. Let baby grab and munch on the pancake. If all is well after a few minutes, offer the bowl of sauce. Show baby how to dip the pancake (or fingers!) in the sauce and paint on a plate or tray.
recipes.howToStore: Apple Nut Pancakes keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days or in the freezer for 2 months. To keep pancakes from sticking in the freezer, allow to cool, lay them in a single layer on a pan, then freeze. Once the pancakes are completely frozen (after about 30 minutes), transfer them to an airtight container to store in the freezer. Best Pancake Sizes for Babies: The goal is for baby to hold the food on their own. If pancakes are small (under 3 inches or 7 ½ cm in diameter), serve them whole. Cut larger pancakes into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together or in bite-sized pieces to hone the pincer grasp.

recipes.title: Edamame Mash + Orange
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) edamame mash + 6-8 orange wedges
recipes.instructions: 1. Place the edamame in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the edamame until the beans are soft, about 2 minutes in the microwave or 5 minutes on the stovetop. The edamame is ready when you can easily mash one with a fork. 2. Use a food processor to blend the edamame, oil, and 1 tbsp (15 ml) of water. Add more oil as needed until it reaches a mostly smooth consistency. A little texture is okay as long as there are no whole beans or clumps. 3. Scoop some mash into baby’s bowl and store the rest for later. Grind sesame seeds into powder to sprinkle on top. 4. Peel the orange rind. Cut the flesh from each membrane. Remove any seeds. Set aside 1 or 2 segments for baby’s meal and store the rest.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the orange segments and edamame mash with a pre-loaded spoon nestled on the side for baby to grab. Let the child self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Edamame mash and cut orange keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. When freezing edamame, store it in small portions (a covered ice cube tray or ¼-cup containers) for up to 2 months. This way, you have easy access to baby-friendly portions at mealtime.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Coconut Fish and Vegetable Curry
ingredients: 1 13 ½-fl oz (400-ml) can unsweetened coconut milk
recipes.instructions: Cut the fish and vegetables. Cut the fish into bite- sized pieces. Remove any bones and skin. Peel and cut the taro into bite-sized pieces. Wash and cut the bell pepper into bite-sized pieces. Peel and finely chop the garlic, ginger, and onion. Cook the curry. Warm the oil in a large pot set on medium heat. When the oil shimmers, add the onion and stir to coat. Cook until the onion has softened, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder and stir to coat. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the taro, bell pepper, coconut milk, and 2 ½ c (600 ml) of water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then lower the heat to create a simmer. Cook the curry for 10 minutes, then add the fish. Continue to cook the curry for 10 minutes more. Juice the lime and stir the juice into the curry. Assemble the meal. Use a slotted spoon or sieve to lift some fish and vegetables from the pot to baby’s bowl for today and reserve some for baby’s meal tomorrow. Season the remaining curry in the pot for yourself with salt to taste. Keep warm while baby’s food cools to room temperature. While cooling, prepare the toppings: thinly slice the hot pepper, finely chop the cilantro leaves and stems, and toast and chop the cashews. Grind a spoonful of cashews into fine powder to sprinkle on baby’s food. Use the rest of the toppings to season your portion.
recipes.howToServe: Flake the fish in baby’s bowl and let baby self-feed on the fish and vegetables. Eat your portion alongside the child to model how it’s done. If baby has trouble picking up the food, mash the vegetables and fish to make it easier to scoop up with hands.
recipes.howToStore: Coconut Fish and Vegetable Curry keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Another Way to Help Baby Eat Curry: Curry is full of flavors that baby can enjoy with you. To help baby self-feed, make a batch of sticky rice to form into balls, then dip the balls in the curry. Let baby munch on the curry rice ball while you enjoy your meal.

meals: White Fish Egg Strips + Curried Taro or Sweet Potato with Ground-Up Walnut
Edamame Mash + Orange + Peanut-Sesame Cauliflower and Snow Pea

recipes.title: White Fish Egg Strips + Curried Taro or Sweet Potato with Ground-Up Walnut
recipes.yield: 6-8 egg strips + ½ c (120 ml) vegetables
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) coconut fish and vegetable curry
recipes.instructions: Prepare the curry. Pull the curry from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 12 | Day 82 | Family Meal to prepare more or substitute canned salmon and steamed sweet potato. Set aside the vegetables to serve as finger food or mash them if you prefer. Grind the walnut into a consistent coarse meal, then sprinkle on top of the vegetables. Cook the egg strips. Flake the fish in a mixing bowl, then crack the eggs into the bowl and whisk to combine with the fish. Warm the oil in an 8-inch non- stick skillet set on medium heat. (If you are using a larger skillet, increase the number of eggs so that the mixture covers the bottom of the pan.) When the oil shimmers, pour in the egg mixture and turn the heat to low. Cover and steam until the eggs are firm and the edges have started to curl, about 5 minutes. Transfer the omelet from the pan to a cutting board. Cut into strips about the width of two adult fingers pressed together. Let cool.
recipes.howToServe: Offer 1 egg strip and the vegetables and let baby self-feed. If baby needs help, pass an egg strip or a pre-loaded spoon in the air for the child to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Egg strips keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Moving on from Mashed Foods: As baby learns to self- feed, it is important to offer foods that hone eating skills. Continuing with mashed food teaches baby that food comes in one texture. As such, start offering finger foods as soon as possible in baby’s transition to solid foods.

recipes.title: Edamame Mash + Orange + Peanut-Sesame Cauliflower and Snow Pea
recipes.instructions: Prepare the edamame. Grab the mashed edamame from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 12 | Day 82 | Meal 2 to prepare more. Prepare the sauce. Whisk the sesame tahini and peanut butter with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps. Pour the sauce into a wide baby bowl. Prepare the vegetables. Grab the raw florets from the refrigerator or freezer. Place them in a steamer basket or a microwave-safe bowl along with the snow peas. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. Cover and steam the florets and snow peas until they have softened slightly, but hold together when pressed, about 3 minutes in the microwave or 6 minutes on the stovetop. Let cool. Cut off the pointy ends of the snow peas and serve the pods whole for baby to munch on.
recipes.howToServe: Drizzle a small spoonful of thinned sauce on the cauliflower florets and stick a snow pea pod in the bowl of sauce so it’s easy for baby to grab. Offer alongside the mashed edamame and orange segments. Let the child self-feed. If baby needs help, dip a floret or snow pea pod in the thinned sauce and pass it in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked vegetables keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. Safely Prepping Snow Peas and Snap Peas: You do not need to pick out the tiny peas inside snow peas. They are so small that they are not a choking risk, and baby’s munching tends to flatten them anyway. Snap peas are a different story: the peas are larger and should be flattened for baby.

recipes.mealType: Family Meal to Share with Baby
recipes.title: Turkey Meatloaf
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) fresh ricotta cheese
recipes.instructions: 1. Defrost the ground meat in the refrigerator the day before you plan to cook. 2. Preheat the oven to 350 F (177 C). Grease a loaf pan or a sheet tray with oil. 3. Wash and dry the lemon and rosemary. Zest the lemon rind and store the lemon for another use. Finely chop the rosemary leaves. Mash and mix the turkey, lemon zest, rosemary, 4. egg, ricotta cheese, breadcrumbs, and spices to form a paste. 5. Transfer the mixture to the loaf pan. If you are using a sheet tray, use your hands to form the paste into a loaf shape on the pan. 6. Bake the meatloaf until meat is fully cooked, between 30 and 45 minutes. Use a food thermometer to check that the internal temperature of the loaf has reached 165 F (74 C). Remove the loaf from the oven and let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes. Slice the loaf into slices about 1 ½ inches (4 cm) thick. Set aside 2 slices for baby to eat today and tomorrow. Season the rest for yourself with salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the meatloaf with applesauce and let baby self-feed while you eat your portion alongside the child to model how it’s done. If baby needs help, pass the slice of meatloaf in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Turkey Meatloaf keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Benefits of Batch Cooking: Double this recipe to make plenty of leftover meatloaf to store in the freezer. You can also use the recipe to make big batch of meatballs or patties. Keeping a batch on hand helps you keep up exposure to common food allergens and saves time when baby is ready to eat.

meals: Mixed Nut Butter Swirl Bowl + Thinly Sliced Strawberries
Applesauce + Broccoli Florets + Turkey Meatloaf

recipes.title: Mixed Nut Butter Swirl Bowl + Thinly Sliced Strawberries
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) yogurt + ½ c (120 ml) berries
ingredients: ½ tsp (3 g) smooth almond butter (honey-free)
½ tsp (3 g) smooth cashew butter (honey-free)
½ tsp (3 g) smooth peanut butter (honey-free)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the berries. Wash and dry the berries. Remove any stems. Decide how to serve the berries. Small, firm strawberries need to be thinly sliced or mashed to reduce choking risk. Alternatively, strawberries may be served whole if they are very large (big enough that baby cannot fit the whole berry in the mouth) and very ripe. To check if large berries are ripe enough to serve whole, use the squish test: press the berry between your fingers to make sure it gives with slight pressure. If you must press hard for the berry to give, it is too firm to serve whole and should be thinly sliced or mashed. butter, and peanut butter with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of yogurt until smooth with no clumps. Scoop the rest of the yogurt into baby’s bowl and swirl in the thinned nut butter. Stick a strawberry or two into the bowl then grind the walnut to sprinkle on top.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the strawberries and yogurt with a spoon stuck into it for baby to grab. Let baby self-feed. If help is needed, pre-load the spoon with yogurt and pass it in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Strawberries keep when loosely sealed in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Slow Down the Spoil: Berries bruise and become moldy at a faster rate when they are wet and tightly packed together. When there is room in the refrigerator, keep them in a paper towel-lined container that is wide enough to store strawberries in a single layer. Alternatively, freeze berries to extend their life.

recipes.title: Applesauce + Broccoli Florets + Turkey Meatloaf
recipes.yield: 1 slice meatloaf + ½ c (120 ml) applesauce + ½ c (120 ml) florets
recipes.instructions: 1. Place the florets in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. 2. Cover and steam the florets. Season the florets with oil and lemon juice. 3. Grab the turkey meatloaf from the refrigerator and cut a slice that is 1 ½ inches (5 cm) thick. If you do not have any leftovers, use the directions on Week 12 | Day 83 | Family Meal to prepare more or substitute flattened pinto beans for some added protein.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the meatloaf, applesauce, and florets and let baby self-feed. To encourage the use of utensils, pre-load a spoon with some applesauce and lay it next to the food for baby to pick up. Alternatively, pass the pre-loaded spoon in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Turkey Meatloaf keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Broccoli florets keep in airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Can Baby Eat Ketchup? Try to wait until after the second birthday. While ketchup is safe for baby if it doesn’t have honey, it can be a slippery slope toward picky eating. Ever see a toddler who just licks the ketchup off food and doesn’t eat the food itself? Most commercial brands of ketchup contain corn syrup to sweeten the taste. Combined with the acidity of tomato and the salty seasonings, it’s a flavor combination that delights the brain.

meals: Cottage Cheese with Guava or Apple
Buttery Sardine Pâté Toasts + Cucumber Strips

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese with Guava or Apple
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) cheese + ½ c (120 ml) guava
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) low-sodium cottage cheese
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash, dry, and halve the fruit. Scoop the pulp and seeds into a blender. 2. If the guava passes the squish test (see below), set aside one half to offer as finger food for baby. Otherwise chop the guava halves and place them in the small blender. Add ½ c (120 ml) of water. Blend until smooth, then press the mixture through a fine- mesh sieve placed over a bowl to remove the seeds. 3. Scoop the cottage cheese into baby’s bowl. Drizzle a spoonful or two of the guava purée on top. 4. Grind the walnut to a consistent coarse meal. Sprinkle the ground-up walnut and hemp seeds on top of the cheese.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the soft guava half and cottage cheese with a pre-loaded spoon on the side. Let baby self-feed, and if help is needed, pass a pre-loaded spoon in the air for the child to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Cut guava and guava purée keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Give Guava A Squish Test: There are many varieties of guava—some crisp like apple and others soft like ripe pear. Firm guava needs to be stewed until soft, while soft guava can be served as finger food. To check if guava is soft enough, give it the squish test: press the guava between your fingers to make sure it gives with slight pressure. If you have to press hard for the guava to give, stew and mash it.

recipes.title: Buttery Sardine Pâté Toasts + Cucumber Strips
recipes.yield: 1 c (240 ml) cucumber + 1 c (240 ml) pâté + 2 toasts
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cucumber. Wash and peel the cucumber. Cut one cucumber into spears for yourself and cut the other cucumber into thin rectangular strips for baby. It is okay to keep the seeds and skin on the vegetable; they get mashed as baby munches but remove them if you prefer. Prepare the pâté. Open the tin and rinse the fish. The tiny bones are edible and full of nutrition but remove them if they make you nervous. Blend the sardines, parsley, green onion, butter, tomato paste, and spices until smooth. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed to ensure all bits get blended into the pâté. Prepare the toast. Toast the bread. Cut one slice into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together for baby, then spread the toast strips with a thin layer of pâté. Season the remaining pâté for yourself with salt to taste, then spread a generous spoonful or two on your slice of toast. Grind the sesame seeds to sprinkle on top with a drizzle of oil.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the cucumber strips with the sardine pâté toast strips. Let baby self-feed while you eat your portion alongside the child to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Sardine Pâté keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Cut cucumber keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. It's Okay to Offer Hot Pepper: The sensory experience helps build familiarity with fiery flavor, which can ease emotions around food during toddlerhood It’s important to start small: just a pinch is enough for baby to taste the heat.

meals: Coconut Chia Seed Pudding with Mixed Nut Butter Swirl + Grapefruit Segments
Spring Vegetable Frittata + Thinly Sliced Strawberries

recipes.title: Coconut Chia Seed Pudding with Mixed Nut Butter Swirl + Grapefruit Segments
recipes.yield: 1 ¾ c (420 ml) pudding + ½ c (120 ml) grapefruit segments
ingredients: ¼ c (60 ml) dry chia seeds
½ tsp (3 g) smooth almond butter (honey-free)
½ tsp (3 g) smooth cashew butter (honey-free)
½ tsp (3 g) smooth peanut butter (honey-free)
2 tsp (4 g) unsweetened desiccated coconut flakes
recipes.instructions: Prepare the pudding. Peel and mash the bananas. Transfer to a small glass jar with a sealed lid. A 3-cup mason jar works perfectly. Add the coconut milk, chia seeds, and spice. Seal then shake vigorously to combine. Place the jar in the refrigerator to chill until the seeds have expanded and the mixture has thickened, at least 1 hour. Shake every 10 minutes or so to emulsify the mixture and help speed up the process. Alternatively, make the pudding the night before serving and let it set overnight in the refrigerator. This way, there is no need to shake. Prepare the nut butter. Whisk the almond butter, cashew butter, peanut butter, and sesame tahini with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water until smooth with no clumps. Scoop some chia seed pudding into baby’s bowl and swirl the thinned nut butter into it. Prepare the grapefruit. Wash the grapefruit, then supreme the citrus. To supreme, first cut off the skin from the top and bottom, then stand the grapefruit on one end, and run your knife down the sides to remove the rind and membrane. After a few minutes, introduce hazelnut: wet your finger then dip it in the hazelnut powder and offer your finger to baby. Let baby taste the flavor, then repeat once or twice, so that the child gets exposure to hazelnut. Let baby continue to self- feed on the sweet potato while you watch for signs of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after 10 minutes, offer more tastes of hazelnut.
recipes.howToStore: Sweet potato spears keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. A Boost of Iron: If you want to round out this meal and boost iron, add a protein on the side, such as bean patties, ground lamb, or smashed chickpeas – your choice. See more iron-rich food ideas.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Veggie Tacos
ingredients: 2 tbsp (16 g) hulled unsalted pumpkin seeds
recipes.instructions: Cut the vegetables. Line a sheet tray with parchment. Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Wash, dry, and halve the peppers, then remove the stem, seeds, and pith and cut the flesh into thin strips. Wash and wipe any grit from the mushroom caps, then cut the caps into strips about the size of your pointer finger. Cook the vegetables. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Coat the mushrooms and vegetables in oil and spices. Evenly space the mushrooms and vegetables on a sheet tray. Roast for 10 minutes, then remove the tray from the oven, flip the mushrooms and vegetables, and roast until the potatoes are easily pierced with a fork, about 10 minutes more. Set aside some mushrooms and vegetables for baby. Season yours with salt to taste. Assemble the tacos. For baby, spread a thin layer of mashed beans on one tortilla, then cut the tortilla into strips about the width of two adult fingers pressed together. Grind some pumpkin seeds into powder to sprinkle on top. Set aside the tortilla strips with some more black beans and baby’s mushrooms and vegetables. Assemble your tacos, adding pumpkin seeds, lime juice, cilantro leaves, and any other seasonings—like hot sauce!
recipes.howToServe: Let baby munch on the strips of mushroom, pepper, and tortilla and practice picking up the beans and bite-sized pieces of sweet potato. As baby self-feeds, eat alongside the child to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked black beans, cooked mushrooms, and cooked bell pepper and sweet potato keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. World of Mushrooms: It’s okay if you would like to offer button mushrooms, cremini mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, and more varieties that have been safely cultivated. If you have a question about a specific variety, search for the mushroom in the free First Foods® database.

meals: Cauliflower Two Ways with Ground-Up Hazelnut
Watermelon Jicama Salad

recipes.title: Cauliflower Two Ways with Ground-Up Hazelnut
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash the cauliflower. Cut off the florets from the primary stem. Set aside 1 c (240 ml) of florets for baby to eat today and store the rest for later. 2. Place the florets in a steamer basket in a pot or a microwave-safe bowl. Add enough water to barely cover the bottom of the pot or bowl. 3. Cover and steam the florets until they have softened slightly, but hold together when pressed, about 3 minutes in the microwave or 6 minutes on the stovetop. 4. Mash small florets (around 1 inch in diameter) and olive oil by hand or in a food processor until smooth. 5. Grind the hazelnut into a fine powder. If the hazelnut has skin, it’s okay to grind the skin with the nut. If you prefer to remove it, rub the nut with a paper towel until the skin slides off.
recipes.howToServe: Let baby munch on large florets. When baby is ready, serve hazelnut: mix the hazelnut powder into a spoonful of mashed cauliflower, then offer the mash on a pre-loaded spoon for baby to grab from you. Let baby continue to munch on the florets as you watch for symptoms of an allergic reaction. If baby seems okay after a few minutes, offer more hazelnut- cauliflower mash.
recipes.howToStore: Cooked cauliflower keeps an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. A Boost of Iron: If you want to round out this meal and boost iron, add a protein on the side, such as bean patties, ground lamb, or smashed chickpeas – your choice. See more iron-rich food ideas.

recipes.title: Watermelon Jicama Salad
ingredients: ½ tsp (1 g) ancho chili powder (optional)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the watermelon. Wash and dry the melon. Cut the melon into quarters, then cut off the rind. Cut the melon into sticks about the size of your pointer finger and remove the seeds. If the size of the sticks makes you nervous, cut the melon into rectangular strips about the thickness of your pinky finger. Set aside 3 c (720 ml) of watermelon sticks and store the rest for later. Prepare the jicama. Peel the skin, then cut the flesh into thin rectangular strips about the thickness of your pinky finger. Assemble the salad. Wash, dry, and finely chop the green onions and cilantro. Place the watermelon, jicama, onion, herb, and chili powder in a mixing bowl. Halve the lime and squeeze the juice over the salad. Toss to coat. Let the salad marinate for 15 minutes so the seasonings infuse the melon and jicama with flavor. Set aside some salad for baby then season the rest for yourself with salt to taste.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the salad to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat your portion alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Watermelon Salad keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. A Boost of Iron :This salad pairs well with iron-rich proteins, such as black-eyed peas, goat cheese, and shredded chicken—perfect fillings for tacos! See more iron-rich food ideas.

meals: Fig or Pear Yogurt Bowl with Ground-Up Hazelnut
Egg-Tofu-Kimchi Fried Rice

recipes.title: Fig or Pear Yogurt Bowl with Ground-Up Hazelnut
recipes.yield: ½ c (120 ml) yogurt + ½ c (120 ml) fruit
recipes.instructions: 1. Wash the figs, then decide how to serve them. 2. Small, firm figs need to be thinly sliced or mashed to reduce the risk. Alternatively, figs may be served whole if they are very large (big enough that baby cannot fit the whole fig in the mouth) and very ripe. 3. To check if figs are ripe enough to serve whole, give the fig the squish test: press the fig between your fingers to make sure it gives with slight pressure. If you must press hard for the fig to give, it is too firm to serve whole and should be thinly sliced or mashed. 4. Scoop the yogurt into baby’s bowl and top with some figs. 5. Grind the hazelnut into a fine powder. If the hazelnut has skin, it’s okay to grind the skin with the nut. If you prefer to remove it, rub the nut with a paper towel until the skin slides off. Sprinkle the ground-up hazelnut on top of baby’s yogurt.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a baby spoon in the yogurt so it is ready for baby to grab. Offer the yogurt and figs and let baby self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Cut figs keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Fig Skins Are Fine: Don’t worry about the skin on fresh figs. The skin not only provides structure for baby as the gums scrape away the flesh, but also builds familiarity with texture, which can ease emotions during the opinionated toddler years to come.

recipes.title: Egg-Tofu-Kimchi Fried Rice
ingredients: 2 ½ c (600 ml) cooked basmati rice
recipes.instructions: Assemble the ingredients. Grab the rice from the refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover, use the directions on Week 9 / Day 57 / Meal 3 to prepare more. Open the package of tofu and cut 7 oz (196 g) of tofu from the main block (1 ounce is approximately equal in size to an adult thumb) then store the rest for later. Rinse, dry, and cut the tofu into bite-sized pieces. Whisk the eggs. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. Cook the fried rice. Warm 1 tbsp (15 ml) of oil in a non-stick skillet set on medium heat. Scramble the eggs, then scrape the eggs onto a plate and return the skillet to the heat. Add another tablespoon of oil, then cook the tofu until golden on all sides. Scrape the tofu onto the plate with the eggs. Add the rest of the oil, then cook the onion and garlic until soft. Increase the heat to medium-high and add the butter. When the butter finishes foaming, stir in the rice and cook, stirring frequently, until the grains are toasted to your liking. Stir in the eggs, tofu, and garden peas to warm the food.
recipes.howToServe: Stick a spoon in the fried rice and offer it with a large piece of kimchi on the side. Let baby self-feed as you eat your portion alongside the child to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Egg-Tofu-Kimchi Fried Rice keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2 days. An open package of firm tofu keeps when sealed in the refrigerator for 3 days. Babies Can Eat Spicy Food: The sensory experience helps build familiarity with fiery flavor, which can ease emotions around food during toddlerhood. It’s important to start small: rinse kimchi to remove some of the heat. This way, baby can taste flavor without the heat overpowering the mouth.

meals: Spiced Cauliflower Florets + Tofu-Egg Strips
Mackerel Salad Sandwich

recipes.title: Spiced Cauliflower Florets + Tofu-Egg Strips
recipes.instructions: Prepare the cauliflower. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Wash and dry the florets. Wash, dry, zest, and juice the lemon. Coat the cauliflower in the oil, 1 tsp (2 g) of zest, and the spice. Evenly space the florets on a sheet tray. Roast until the florets starts to brown and a knife easily inserts into the thickest stalk, about 20 minutes. Remove the tray from the oven and set aside some large florets for baby’s meal and season with a small drizzle of lemon juice. Grind the hazelnut into a fine powder. If the hazelnut has skin, it’s okay to grind the skin with the nut. If you prefer to remove it, rub the nut with a paper towel until the skin slides off. Sprinkle the ground-up hazelnut on top of the florets. Prepare the egg strips. Grab the tofu from the refrigerator and cut 1 oz (28 g) from the main block (1 ounce is approximately equal in size to an adult thumb) and store the rest. Finely chop the tofu. Crack the eggs into the mixing bowl. Add the whole milk and tofu. Whisk to combine the ingredients. Warm the butter in an 8-inch non-stick skillet set on medium heat. (If you are using a larger skillet, increase the number of eggs so that the mixture covers the bottom of the pan.) When the butter finishes foaming, pour in the egg mixture and turn the heat to low. Cover and steam until the eggs are firm and the edges have started to curl, about 5 minutes. Transfer the omelet from the pan to a cutting board. Cut into strips about
recipes.howToServe: Offer the florets and some egg strips and let baby self-feed.
recipes.howToStore: Spiced cauliflower florets and tofu-egg strips keep in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3 days. An open package of firm tofu keeps when sealed in the refrigerator for 3 days.

recipes.title: Mackerel Salad Sandwich
ingredients: ½ c (120 ml) baby spinach leaves (optional)
recipes.instructions: 1. Open the tins and rinse the fish with water to remove some of the sodium. Tiny bones are edible and full of nutrition but remove them if they make you nervous. 2. Set aside 1 fish to serve whole. Mash and mix the remaining fish with mayonnaise and spices to make a paste. Finely chop the parsley and stir the herb into the salad. 3. Set aside 1 tbsp (15 ml) of salad for baby and season the rest for yourself with mustard and salt to taste. 4. Toast the bread until it is lightly browned, then cut 1 slice into strips about the size of two adult fingers pressed together for baby. Spread a thin layer of the mackerel salad on the bread. Use the rest to make yourself a sandwich with baby spinach and sliced tomato.
recipes.howToServe: Offer some whole fish, tomato wedges, and toast strips to baby and let the child self-feed. Eat your sandwich alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Mackerel Salad keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Skip the Tuna: Try to use mackerel, sardines, or another low-mercury fish as a substitute for tuna in tuna salad sandwiches. Tuna is very high in mercury and overfished around the world.

meals: Pumpkin Spice Swirl Bowl with Ground-Up Granola + Quartered Blackberries
Buttery Cod and Potato Bake
allergens: Tree Nut (Almond, Cashew, Hazelnut, Pecan, Walnut)

recipes.title: Pumpkin Spice Swirl Bowl with Ground-Up Granola + Quartered Blackberries
recipes.yield: ⅓ c (80 ml) berries + ½ c (120 ml) yogurt
recipes.instructions: 1. Grab the ground-up granola from your refrigerator. If you do not have any leftover granola, use the directions on Week 13 | Day 90 | Meal 1 to prepare more. 2. Grind the hazelnuts into a fine powder. If the hazelnut has skin, it’s okay to grind the skin with the nut. If you prefer to remove it, rub the nut with a paper towel until the skin slides off. Mix the ground-up hazelnut into the ground-up granola. 3. Combine the pumpkin purée and spices. Adjust the amount of spices to taste. 4. Scoop the yogurt into baby’s bowl and swirl in the spiced pumpkin purée. Sprinkle the ground-up granola on top. 5. Wash the blackberries, then quarter them lengthwise. If you are using blueberries, flatten them with your thumb or a fork.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the quartered blackberries and the yogurt with a spoon stuck into it for baby to grab. Let baby self-feed. If help is needed, pre-load the spoon and pass it in the air for baby to grab from you.
recipes.howToStore: Blackberries keep when loosely sealed in the refrigerator for 3 days or in the freezer for 2 months. Slow Down the Spoil: Berries bruise and become moldy at a faster rate when they are wet and tightly packed together. When there is room in the refrigerator, keep them in a paper towel-lined container that is wide enough to store blackberries in a single layer. Alternatively, freeze berries to extend their life.

recipes.title: Buttery Cod and Potato Bake
recipes.instructions: Start the bake. Defrost the fish in the refrigerator the day before you plan to cook. If you have one large fillet, cut it crosswise to create smaller fillets about 2 in (5 cm) wide. Preheat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and onions. Toss the vegetables in a baking dish. Warm the milk and 6 tbsp (112 g) of butter, then pour the mixture over the potatoes. Toss to coat. Sprinkle spice on top. Evenly space the potatoes and onions in the dish; it’s okay if they overlap. If necessary, add more milk so the potatoes are nearly covered. Place the dish in the oven. Prepare the fish. While the potatoes bake, melt the medium-high heat. Stir in the breadcrumbs and cook until toasted. After 30 minutes of baking, remove the dish from the oven, lay the cod on top of the potatoes, and add breadcrumbs on top. Return the dish to the oven. Finish the bake. Bake until the fish is fully cooked, between 10 and 15 minutes depending on the thickness. It is ready when a food thermometer inserted into the thickest fish has reached 145 F (63 C). Remove the dish from the oven. Set aside some fish and potatoes for baby. Break baby’s fish into large flakes about the size of your thumb. Season the rest of the food for yourself with salt to taste. Keep your food warm while baby’s food cools.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the flaked fish and potatoes with a pre-loaded age-appropriate fork for baby to grab. Let baby self-feed while you eat your portion alongside baby to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Buttery Cod and Potato Bake keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days

meals: Hard-Boiled Egg Two Ways + Mixed Nut Butter "Paint" with Rainbow Pepper Spears
100 Days Pizza Party
allergens: Tree Nut (Almond, Cashew, Hazelnut, Pecan, Walnut)

recipes.title: Hard-Boiled Egg Two Ways + Mixed Nut Butter "Paint" with Rainbow Pepper Spears
recipes.yield: 2 eggs + ¼ c (60 ml) paint + ¾ c (180 ml) pepper
ingredients: 1 tsp (5 g) smooth mixed nut butter (honey-free)
recipes.instructions: Prepare the egg. Use the directions on Week 2 | Day 8 to hard-boil the eggs. Once the eggs are finished cooking and cool, peel the shell of one egg and store the other one for later in the week. Cut the peeled egg into bite-sized pieces (about the size of your knuckle) to help baby hone the pincer grasp. Mash 1 or 2 pieces with the yogurt, then spread the mixture on a slice of toasted bread. Cut the bread into strips. Prepare the paint. Whisk the mixed nut butter, tahini, and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of warm water until smooth— like paint—in a baby bowl that is wide enough to reach inside. Grind the peanuts and hazelnuts into a fine powder. Mix the ground-up nuts into the paint. Prepare the peppers. Wash the peppers. Cut one half from each pepper and store the other halves for another use. Cut the pepper halves into thin spears. Stick a couple of spears in the bowl of “paint” and serve the rest on the side.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the quartered hard-boiled egg, toast strips, pepper spears, and bowl of paint. Let the child self-feed. Show baby how to dip the pepper spears in the sauce and paint on the plate.
recipes.howToStore: Hard-boiled eggs keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 1 week. Cut peppers keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. What's in Mixed Nut Butter: Mixed nut butter is an easy way to maintain regular exposure to common food allergens, but exactly which tree nuts are used depends on the brand. Choose brands that have tree nuts already introduced—or use the directions from Week 14 | Day 94 | Meal 1 to prepare your own.

recipes.title: 100 Days Pizza Party
recipes.instructions: 1. It’s time to treat yourself. You made it through 100 days of starting solids! Pour yourself a nice drink to enjoy while you wait for pizza to be ready. 2. In its whole form, pizza with globs of melted cheese is a choking hazard, but good news: it can be deconstructed to safely share with baby. 3. Cut off most of a pizza slice so that you are left with just the crust for baby. The crust’s shape and consistency are fantastic for helping baby create a mental map of mouth and advance oral-motor skills. It’s okay if there is a little sauce on the crust, but it is important to pick off any loose toppings and globs of cheese to minimize the choking risk. 4. Cut toppings into age-appropriate sizes for baby. Toppings come in all shapes and sizes—some saltier and sweeter than others, and some that come with a higher risk. Check which toppings are okay for the child’s age and how to cut or modify them using the free First Foods® database. 5. Take-out pizza is way too salty to regularly share with baby, but on occasion, it’s a great choice. To minimize the amount of salt, make your own pizza from scratch. Search the free First Foods® database for homemade rainbow pizza—a great activity for toddlers.
recipes.howToServe: Offer the crust with some room-temperature marinara or tomato sauce for dipping. Let baby gnaw on the crust and paint with the sauce. As baby self-feeds, enjoy your pizza to model how it’s done.
recipes.howToStore: Leftover pizza keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 days. Best Pizza for Babies: A classic margherita pizza with fresh mozzarella cheese, plain tomato sauce, and a thick crust is a great pick, but the “best pizza” for baby is the one that connects to your culture, family, and traditions. Pick your favorite and be mindful of sodium: most pizza is very salty!
